    **F13 LOW, ✅ FIXED on `fix/428-attestation-tail`.** `federation_admission` skips a pinned contract naming a provider outside `plans` instead of refusing, in a function whose stated posture is refuse-as-one-unit. **Reproduced first** over a real `consumer_surface` pin and a real compiled provider: `federation_admission({'db': provider}, contracts=[(surface, 'db')])` admitted, and the SAME call with the provider named `typo-db` also admitted, with zero refusals, because `plans.get(provider_id) is None` hit a bare `continue`. **Fixed:** the missing provider is now a refusal of its own kind, `REFUSE_UNKNOWN_PROVIDER = 'contract-provider-not-in-update'`, and the reason names what the update DOES carry so the author can see the typo or the dropped composition. A pin the update cannot check is not a pin the update satisfied, and all-or-nothing cannot mean all of the ones it happened to be able to look at. One regression test in `tests/test_deploy_118.py`.
    **NEGATIVE RESULTS.** No reachable second preimage in `_canonical_bytes` on the deploy path (the conflations that exist need non-string keys or tuples, unreachable from `ir/ir.json`); NFC/NFD differ; `1.0` vs `1` differ; omitted vs present-and-null differ; injected, dropped or reordered fields all break the MAC; no field is outside the signed body except the signature; HMAC has no length-extension exposure; `hmac.compare_digest` throughout. The re-hash-on-receive DISCIPLINE is sound (`SELF_DECLARED_IGNORED` members really are never read, `composition_hash` and the artifact facet are genuinely recomputed from the receiver's disk, a bound-but-missing facet fails closed). The capability ceiling is a raw string set-difference that fails CLOSED on a spelling mismatch, so no parameter-drop or cone-widening bypass exists; the defect is the fail-open when the projection is missing. `plan_add_report` re-verifies at add time; `plan_drift` refuses drift when a pin EXISTS; `binding_mismatch` treats bound-but-absent as tamper; `verify_required=True` with a key really does filter a tampered attestation.

429. **THE SELF-HOST ORACLES CANNOT CATCH WHAT THE CORPUS DOES NOT EXERCISE, AND THIS RECURRED THREE TIMES IN ONE DAY (2026-09-02).** Item 391 states this in the abstract ("a feature the corpus does not exercise leaves the oracle green while the self-host lacks it") and item 417 records the largest instance (the missing type layer). This item records that it is not a one-off but the dominant failure mode of the byte-agreement gate, with three same-day instances, two of which ran in the OPPOSITE direction from the one 391 anticipates.
    (a) **✅ BOTH DEFECTS FIXED; RECORDED HERE AS A STRATEGY OBSERVATION, NOT AN OPEN FINDING.** **The self-host was RIGHT and the reference was WRONG (twice).** Fixing the callee-subtree defect (`emission_analysis._calls_in` pruning the entire callee subtree, roadmap 421 F1 territory), the implementer found `selfhost/checker.rvl::call_calls` already had the CORRECT shape: `calls_in(tg, acc)` on the target, then `push(cn)` for the name. The reference was the divergent one. Independently, fixing the Unicode-identifier defect, the implementer found `selfhost/lexer.rvl` already REFUSED all three exploits (`ｓend`, `ﬁlter`, `x²`), because `Str.is_alpha`/`is_alnum` are ASCII-only by spec while the reference used Python's full-Unicode `str.isalpha()`. In both cases the oracle was green because both sides agreed on the corpus, not because both sides were right. **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** nothing to fix under this letter; it is evidence for the item's thesis, and its exit lives in the numbered Exit list below.
    (b) **✅ PORTED (this is the item-421-F3 port; see 429(c) for the sibling that was NOT closed by it).** **A port the oracle did not demand, and would never have demanded.** The non-injective keyword mangling fix (`lambda` and a distinct `lambda_` collapsing to one emitted name) found the SAME defect in five self-host emitters (`emit_py`, `emit_ts`, `emit_go`, `emit_java`, `emit_rust`). The oracles were green WITHOUT the port because the covered corpus contains no keyword-twin pairs. The implementer checked the sources directly rather than trusting the gate, ported the fix, and PROVED the port was load-bearing by adding an injectivity assertion to the pristine tree and watching it fail. A byte-agreement gate cannot ask for a fix to a case the corpus never spells. **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** the injective rule is present in all five self-host emitters, `selfhost/emit_rust.rvl:137-141` among them. Do not read this as closing 429(c), which is a different defect in the reserved-word SET.
    (c) **❌ STILL OPEN, RE-VERIFIED IN SOURCE ON `bd0f4d19`.** **A live sibling, unfixed and invisible to the gate.** `backends/rust/emit.py` mirrors `_RUST_RESERVED | _EMITTER_RESERVED` while `selfhost/emit_rust.rvl` mirrors only `_RUST_RESERVED`, so `ctx`/`config`/`root`/`plugin` diverge. Latent for exactly the same reason, and the oracle will not catch it. **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** `selfhost/emit_rust.rvl:146-151` `mangle` still lists ONLY the Rust keywords, while `backends/rust/emit.py:86` carries `_EMITTER_RESERVED = {"ctx", "config", "root", "plugin"}` and `:732` escapes against BOTH sets. The item-421-F3 injectivity port DID land in `selfhost/emit_rust.rvl:137-141` (that is (b) above), which is exactly why this reads as done at a glance and is not: the RULE was ported, the SOURCE-OF-TRUTH SET was not. A revl local named `ctx` still emits `ctx_` from the reference and `ctx` from the self-host.
    (d) **◑ THE EMIT HALF LANDED, THE STAGE BELOW IT DID NOT.** **A FIFTH instance, same day, found while fixing item 421 F6 (2026-09-02).** The F6 fix marks secrets in the EMITTED program at both ends: `_revl_mark_secret(p)` on a provide-method parameter its service declares `Secret[T]`, and a result marker on a `Secret[T]`-returning extern. `selfhost/emit_py.rvl` can emit NEITHER: `method_lines` (:1067) receives only the method IR node and `provide_lines` never threads the services table, so it cannot see `params[i].secret`, and `_emit_externs` (:687) has no return-side marking. That is a REAL divergence for any `Secret[T]` composition: the self-host emitter produces a program that does not redact. It is invisible because `tests/fixtures/emit_py_corpus/` contains no `Secret[` at all, so the oracle is green and says nothing. This is category (ii) again, and the consequence is a SECURITY one rather than a cosmetic one, which is the argument for (3) below being a real exit condition and not a nicety. **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** the two paragraphs headed "(5), what landed" and "(5) found while doing it" below carry this letter's verdict: the self-host emit-side port landed, and the frontend stage below it followed on `fix/selfhost-frontend-secret-marking` — the DECLARATION marking is carried, so a fully native compile of a `Secret[T]` document now matches the reference byte for byte on both wired tiers. What stays open under this letter is not the marking but the reference FLOW analysis, which the self-host still does not have and which this letter never asked for.
    **What this changes about the strategy.** The differential oracles were adopted to prevent SILENT DIVERGENCE, and they do prevent it on the covered corpus. What they cannot do is (i) tell you which side is correct when both agree and both are wrong, (ii) demand a feature or a fix the corpus does not reach, or (iii) notice that two sides mirror DIFFERENT source-of-truth sets. Item 391's standing "does this need a self-host port?" step is necessary but not sufficient, because it fires on new FEATURES and two of these three were BUG FIXES to shared logic.
    **Exit:** (1) a standing rule that any fix to logic mirrored in `selfhost/*` is checked against the self-host source DIRECTLY, not via the oracle, and the check is recorded in the change; (2) when the reference and the self-host disagree, treat it as an open question about which is right rather than assuming the reference (it lost twice today); (3) corpus families that FAIL while a known gap exists, per item 417's exit, generalized beyond the type layer to the categories above; (4) fix the `_EMITTER_RESERVED` divergence in (c); (5) ✅ DONE (`fix/429e-selfhost-secret-redaction`) add a `Secret[` family to `emit_py_corpus/` and port the (d) markings, since a self-host emitter that silently does not redact is a security divergence, not a parity nicety. Relates to 391 (parity), 417 (the type-layer gap), 146 (full self-host).
    **(5), what landed.** Reproduced first on one input: the reference emitted `@_revl_secret_result` above `mint_token`, `_revl_mark_secret(token)` / `_revl_mark_secret(a, b)` at the head of the marked provide methods, and both names in the `from runtime import` line; `selfhost/emit_py.rvl` emitted none of the three. New corpus entry `tests/fixtures/emit_py_corpus/secrets.rvl` covers BOTH ends and the negative cases in one document (a `Secret[Str]`-returning extern beside a plain one, a one-secret method, a three-param method with two non-adjacent secrets, an unmarked method, and an empty-bodied marked method, which is the one branch where the mark REPLACES the `pass`). It was added FIRST and seen to FAIL (`1 failed, 22 passed`) before any emitter change, per exit (3): a corpus entry that was never seen to red proves nothing. The port threads the SERVICES table from `emit_py_src` down through `component_body` -> `emit_body_steps` -> `body_step` -> `provide_lines` -> `method_lines`, which is what the self-host structurally could not reach before (`method_lines` had only the method IR node); the receiver-side stamp is read BY INDEX off the service's declared params (`method_secret_params`) since a method's surface names may differ from the declared ones, and the return-side stamp comes off `externs[i].secret_return`. Both imports are gated on exactly the conditions that emit their call (`body_has_secret_param` walks `if` branches like `body_has_timer`; `secret_result` is gated from the extern list, outside any component, as the reference gates it), so every secret-free document stays byte-identical. **Ablation:** with the corpus entry kept and ONLY `selfhost/emit_py.rvl` reverted, `secrets.rvl` reds again and the other 22 stay green, so the port is load-bearing and not incidentally satisfied.
    **(5) found while doing it, NOW CLOSED for the DECLARATION marking (`fix/selfhost-frontend-secret-marking`): the self-host had NO TAINT STAGE AT ALL, one stage earlier.** Adding `secrets.rvl` to `emit_py_corpus/` also feeds `tests/test_selfhost_lower_ir.py` (which globs the whole directory) and `tests/test_selfhost_compile.py`, and the native LOWERING gate diverged too: it renders `"type": "Secret[Str]"` verbatim and emits neither the `params[i].secret` stamp nor `secret_return`. The cause is bigger than this item: `Untrusted`, `Trusted` and `Secret` appear ZERO times in `selfhost/lower.rvl` and ZERO times in `selfhost/checker.rvl`, while `src/revl/taint.py` strips all three qualifiers and leaves the stamps the backends read. Porting one qualifier's stamps alone would be a partial taint stage, so this is RECORDED rather than patched: the two affected projections carry a STRICT xfail naming the gap (`TAINT_QUALIFIED_GAP`), which is red for a named reason today and XPASSes loudly the day a taint stage lands, rather than the fixture being dropped from the corpus. The emit_py port above is unaffected, since every emitter consumes the reference IR, which carries the stamps; what the gap does mean is that a FULLY native compile (`selfhost/compile.rvl`, item 224) would hand the ported emitter an IR with no stamps and get no redaction, so the native pipeline is not secret-safe until the taint stage is ported. One more incidental: the self-host parser does not accept a scoped `extern emission[cap.op] fn` (`BAD|expected fn after extern` from `test_native_gate_admits_the_whole_emit_surface`), so the fixture declares its `Secret[Str]`-returning extern `pure`; `taint.py` sets `secret_return` off the declared return qualifier alone, so the marking is exercised either way. **CLOSED for the declaration-side marking.** `selfhost/lower.rvl` now carries the qualifier surgery (`taint_strip`, the recursive `taint_mentions_secret`, `taint_secret_witness`) and stamps the four IR positions a backend consumes: `params[i].secret` on an extern, a module fn and a service operation; `secret_return` and `secret_witness` on an extern; and a config field's `secret`. All three qualifiers are stripped, since leaving `Untrusted[T]` standing as a TYPE NAME is wrong the same way `Secret[T]` was. The discipline was followed in order: `tests/fixtures/emit_py_corpus/secrets_nested.rvl` (a nested `Result[Secret[Str], Str]` return, a `Secret[T]` module-fn parameter, an `Opt[Secret[Str]]` service parameter and a `Secret[T]` config field — the four positions `secrets.rvl` does not reach) was added FIRST and the `TAINT_QUALIFIED_GAP` xfail removed, giving 6 named failures across services / component headers / externs / functions before any `.rvl` change. `tests/test_selfhost_compile.py`'s strict xfail then XPASSED and is gone: a `Secret[T]` document now compiles FULLY natively to bytes identical to the reference compile on both wired tiers, so the native pipeline is no longer the hole this paragraph described. **NOT ported, deliberately:** the reference's FLOW analysis — the origin lattice, the `confidential` / `secret` origins, `Untrusted`/`Trusted` sinks and sources, `endorse` and the checked-parser declassifiers, and the G9 refusals. The self-host has a MARKING, not a taint analysis; nothing mints an origin and nothing refuses a program.
    **(5) sibling survey (the (b)-shaped question: is any OTHER tier blind the same way?).** No. `secret` appears 38 times in `backends/python/emit.py` and ZERO times in the ts/go/java/rust/wasm reference emitters, and zero times in `selfhost/emit_{ts,go,java,rust,wasm}.rvl`. Checked by running each tier's reference emitter and its self-host port over the same `Secret[Str]`-receiver composition: neither side of any non-py tier emits anything mentioning a secret, so there is no self-host DIVERGENCE there and those oracles are honest. What the survey does show is a different gap, one tier up and NOT of the 429 class: the F6 marking (and item 256's `_revl_secret` bound-secret injection with it) is PYTHON-TIER ONLY, so an emitted ts/go/java/rust/wasm program does not redact at all. That is reference-side coverage, not self-host parity, and it belongs to whoever takes 421 F6 cross-tier. (Incidentally observed and NOT touched: go and wasm already diverge from their references on this component shape, identically with the `Secret[...]` qualifier removed, so it is a pre-existing out-of-corpus shape unrelated to secrets.) **SURVEY REDONE ON SOURCE 2026-09-02 (#234), AND THE COUNT ABOVE IS NOW OUT OF DATE.** The cross-tier work the paragraph handed to "whoever takes 421 F6 cross-tier" happened: `secret` is no longer zero in the non-py reference emitters. ts carries `host.secretResult` / `host.markSecret` / `, secret: true`; go carries `revlSecretResult`, `revlMarkSecret`, a `_declares_secret` mode gate that reads a config field, and a `secret_witness` WAL referent; rust, java and wasm each carry the `secret_witness` WAL referent. Re-diffing every self-host emitter against its reference counterpart site by site, rather than trusting a green byte-agreement oracle, found ONE emitter with a reference site inside its own covered surface and no code for it: `selfhost/emit_py.rvl` consumed `secret_return` and a method's `params[i].secret` but had no config-field site at all, so `_revl_ConfigSchema([..])` went out without the `secret=[..]` argument the runtime redacts the `<name>.config` trace line from. Ported in #234, corpus first: `secrets_nested.rvl` was in neither the emit_py oracle corpus nor the fully-native compile corpus, was added to both, and was seen to red on exactly that argument before the port. Every other non-py site is out of its self-host emitter's covered surface rather than missing from it — `revlMarkSecret` and the `_SECRET_MODE` config scan sit in the live-component and placement worlds `selfhost/emit_go.rvl` lists as deferred, and every `secret_witness` site is `--record` WAL emission, which no self-host emitter emits at all. #234 also found and fixed a second, unrelated defect the same corpus addition reddened: `uses_builtin_result` in `selfhost/emit_py.rvl` mirrored only the `adt`/`match`/checked-division walk and neither of `_uses_builtin_result`'s two extern clauses, so a document whose only Result is an extern's declared return emitted a module that references `Ok`/`Err` and never defines them.

430. ✅ **THE ROOT `tests/` SUITE HAD NEVER RUN WITH THE CORDIS-PY RUNTIME IN CI, SO 398 TESTS EXECUTED NOWHERE (2026-09-02).** `pytest tests/ -q` appeared in exactly one CI job, `frontend`, which installs `pip install -e ".[test]"` and therefore has no cordis-py. Every test in `tests/` guarded on `importlib.util.find_spec("cordis")` skipped there, and no other job picked them up: `backend-python` runs with cwd `backends/python`, so its `tests/` is `backends/python/tests/`, a different suite; `backend-rust` runs one file from the root suite (`test_gate_crate_admit.py`) and `conformance` another (`test_conformance_validate.py`). `make pre-merge` has the same shape locally (`tools/pre_merge.sh` runs the root suite under the plain `.venv`). 48 files in `tests/` carry that guard. Measured on the merge base: the runtime-less suite runs 6399 tests and skips 521 (381 of them on cordis-py); with the runtime it runs 6796, so **398 tests across 81 modules had never executed in CI**, including the whole of the standing-approval, standing-revoke, fault-activation, session-commit/fork, undo, auto-mocks, witnessed-teardown and self-extending surfaces. **Fixed:** a `frontend-cordis` CI job runs the root suite under `backends/python/.venv/bin/python` after `sh backends/python/setup.sh`. The `frontend` job is unchanged and still gates the separate, real property that the suite is green on a checkout with NO runtime. **The exclusion list is EMPTY.** The first full run under the runtime was green on all 6796, with 144 skips left, none of them on cordis-py except the one test that asserts the runtime-less path (macOS, py3.14, cordis-py at the pinned `1c5e6f1`); nothing had to be deselected, xfailed or weakened. If a failure appears on the Linux/py3.12 runner, enumerate it as a `--deselect` in the job with a reason and list it here rather than narrowing the job's path. **Also fixed:** `tests/test_r2_allowlist_key_binding.py::test_forbidden_grant_still_refuses_a_named_decider` was red on `main` because it drives `Gate.load` with no guard (the same defect as `test_mcp_authoring_trust.py`, fixed at 258542af the same day); and `tests/conftest.py` now carries a `pytest_runtest_makereport` net that turns the runtime's "the cordis-py runtime is not installed" failure into a skip **only when `find_spec("cordis") is None`**, so a third forgotten guard cannot red `frontend` while the same error still fails loudly wherever the runtime is present. The net is deliberately second: without `frontend-cordis` it would have hidden the lost coverage instead of protecting anything. Relates to 327 (the per-backend drift gap, the same failure mode one tier up) and 419a.

431. **THE NEW `frontend-cordis` JOB WENT RED ON ITS FIRST REAL RUN, AND BOTH CAUSES ARE WORTH KEEPING (2026-09-02).** Item 430 added a CI job running the root suite under the cordis-py runtime. It was green locally and red on the runner, in two different ways, neither of which the local run could have shown.
    (a) ✅ FIXED. **64 `[go]` failures: a toolchain guard that admits the wrong toolchain.** `tests/test_cross_tier_execution.py` and `tests/test_conformance_validate.py` execute emitted Go against the PINNED stc-go runtime, and they decide whether to run from whether a `go` binary answers on PATH. `ubuntu-latest` preinstalls one, so on the new job they did not skip: they ran against the runner's default Go and failed the pinned build (`go emitted code its own toolchain rejects`). `backend-go` never hit this because it pins Go 1.26 with `actions/setup-go@v5`. Fixed by pinning the same version in `frontend-cordis`. **The general shape is worth noting: a presence check (`is there a go?`) is not a compatibility check (`is it the pinned one?`), and the failure mode is a job that runs tests it should have skipped rather than one that skips tests it should have run.** That is the mirror image of item 430's own defect, discovered by fixing it.
    (b) ✅ **FIXED, AND THE PRODUCT QUESTION IS SETTLED: NO, a witnessed `write` must not be atomic against a concurrent unlink, it must be TRUTHFUL** (`backends/python/revl_fs_workspace.py`, `stdlib/fs.rvl`, `tests/test_fs_confinement_escapes.py`; decided and implemented with item 422 F5/F6/F7, which is where it was filed to land). The original symptom: `tests/test_fs_confinement_escapes.py::test_a_concurrent_writer_cannot_divert_a_write_out_of_the_root` raised `FileNotFoundError` out of `mod.write` on 3.11, from the undo-snapshot read rather than the confinement check, and the security property the test pins (no write ever reaches an inode outside the root) held throughout. **What the reproduction found is that the transient was the lesser half of the defect.** Driving the exact window deterministically (unlink the leaf after `open_confined_write` holds the fd, before either `snapshot_preimage` or `write_through`) showed `write` returning **`Ok`** with a witness naming a path that does NOT hold the bytes: the fd reached the inode the check admitted, the unlink made that inode an ORPHAN, and so the discharge descriptor enumerated a successful witnessed write of a file that was gone while the registered undo stood ready to restore a preimage over a forward mutation that never became visible. Confinement held; the RESULT lied. **Why not atomic.** Create-or-replace under the directory fd is a LIVENESS promise this jail cannot honour: the workspace writer is untrusted by premise (that is the whole reason the jail exists), so whatever a recreate puts back can be unlinked again the instant after, and the guarantee would be true only against a polite racer. It also costs something real, a rename-based write reintroduces the by-name step the directory-fd walk exists to remove, and it would silently break the `EMULTILINK` posture by replacing the NAME rather than refusing a multiply-linked target. What the reversibility story actually needs is not that the write survive an adversary but that the WITNESS be true, because the witness is what the undo consumes and what the audit surface enumerates. **What landed instead.** `confirm_landed` re-walks to the parent through the same directory fds and compares `(st_dev, st_ino)` on the leaf against the fd that was written; a parted name is `Err(ERACE)` naming what the author can do next (item 274), and an `Err` registers no inverse. `discard_write` now clears the preimage sidecar and removes the created leaf ONLY when it still holds our inode, removing by name after a lost race deleted the COMPETING writer's file, which was a second bug the fix surfaced. `snapshot_preimage` refuses with `ESNAPSHOT` rather than raising, since a write with no preimage is not reversible and the honest outcome is to refuse before a byte is written. Note the answer to the question as asked is "surface the transient", but only because it is surfaced as a TYPED `Err` on the declared `Result`, a raw exception escaping the body was never acceptable, and item 422 F6's totality work is what makes the typed form reachable. **The test is tightened, not loosened**: the `except OSError` tolerance is REMOVED and the call now asserts a typed result, so a raw exception there is a real regression rather than a transient; both leak assertions are unchanged.

432. **WASM CODEGEN PERFORMANCE AUDIT: THE CANONICAL-ABI BOUNDARY COPIES EVERY STRING BYTE THROUGH AN INTERPRETED LOOP, AND 85% OF EVERY EMITTED MODULE IS UNREACHABLE (2026-09-02).** Audit of the code the wasm backend GENERATES, against what a competent wasm author writes for the same semantics. Harness committed at `bench/codegen/wasm/` (`run.py`, `probe_heap.py`, `harness.py`, `programs/`, `results.json`) and re-runnable standalone. **No timings were taken and none should be quoted from this item**: the audit machine was carrying about a dozen concurrent agents, so every number below is load-independent by construction. The executed measure is wasmtime **fuel**, an exact count of executed wasm operations found by bisecting `-W fuel=N`; the rest are module byte sizes, reachability, and static allocation and copy counts. Executed against wasmtime 47.0.3 and `wasm-tools` through the component model on macOS arm64; the emitter was NOT edited, each proposed fix was A/B'd as a hand-written rewrite of the emitted WAT, and `run.py` refuses to report a variant that does not return exactly what the baseline returns.
    (a) **`$__canon_lift_str` copies a `Str` byte by byte in a wasm loop, and the copy is not needed at all.** Every `Str` entering the module through the canonical boundary goes through a five-instruction-per-byte loop. Measured slope: **19 fuel per argument byte**. Swapping the loop for the `memory.copy` the same module already uses in `$str_concat`, `$str_slice` and `$list_push` gives **1 fuel/byte** (`echo` of a 4 KiB string: 77900 to 4174 fuel, 73726 saved per call). Better, the copy is removable: a canonical `string` param reaches a linear-memory callee in memory the callee itself handed out through `cabi_realloc`, so if `cabi_realloc` reserves 8 bytes of headroom and returns `p+8`, the incoming bytes already sit exactly where the internal `[u32 len][bytes]` layout wants them and lifting is one store of the length. Measured: **0 fuel/byte, 58 fuel flat at every string length from 16 B to 4 KiB**, and the component still round-trips `"hello"` correctly. Emitter line: `backends/wasm/canonical.py:680` (`base_helpers`). BLAST RADIUS: the four `golden/*.wat` byte-identical oracles; `canonical.py` is not mirrored in `selfhost/emit_wasm.rvl`, so no self-host port. The zero-copy form must be gated on the argument having come from this module's own `cabi_realloc`, which is the ABI's contract for an indirect param but should be asserted in the fix rather than assumed. **FIXED 2026-09-02** (`fix/432acf-wasm-canonical-copies`, f99df69a, `backends/wasm/canonical.py`). `cabi_realloc` now reserves 8 bytes below every buffer it hands out and `$__canon_lift_str` is one store of the length. RE-MEASURED on the committed harness, baseline before vs baseline after: `echo` **19.000 to 0.000 fuel/byte**, flat **49 fuel** at 16 B, 256 B and 4 KiB alike (77900 to 49 at 4 KiB, 77851 saved per call); `greet` 21 to 2 fuel/byte; `concat6` 58 to 20. The `cabi_realloc` provenance is CHECKED, not assumed: the zero-copy path is gated on `$ptr` lying at or above this module's `$alloc` floor, and every other pointer, including the any-aligned-address a host may pass for a zero-length string, takes a bulk `memory.copy` instead, so the lift can never write below a buffer it was not given room under. That guard is 4 fuel flat per lift, which is why `echo` lands at 49 rather than the audit's unguarded 45. Cost: +20 B core.wasm on the string programs, the fallback keeping `$alloc_str` reachable; (b) is where module size gets fixed. Goldens regenerated: the three that carry the boundary (`canonical_echoer`, `canonical_aggregates`, `canonical_service` `.core.wat`); the `.wit` files did not move, the interface being unchanged. SELF-HOST: verified in the source, not through the oracle (item 429). `cabi_realloc`, `__canon_*` and the canonical return area occur ZERO times anywhere under `selfhost/`; `emit_wasm.rvl:1365` mirrors emit.py's `$__hp`/`$alloc_str`/`$str_concat` prelude, which is (b)'s and (d)'s blast radius, not this one's. No port.
    (b) **The linear-memory helper prelude is emitted unconditionally, so 27 to 30 of every 32 to 34 emitted functions are unreachable from any export.** `emit.py:2732` `_helper_funcs()` returns a fixed list of 16 memory helpers, and `emit.py:2750` appends 10 arithmetic and 3 list helpers, all of them whenever the module needs a memory at all. Only `$f64_to_str`, `$str_index_of`, `$str_split` and `$str_join` are gated on use (`emit.py:2129-2143`), and that gating is exactly the pattern the rest should follow. Measured core module sizes, baseline versus dead-code-pruned: `echo` **3483 to 503 B (85.6% smaller)**, `scalar` (an `Int` doubler, which still drags in `$str_concat`, `$str_to_int`, `$int_to_str`, the codepoint walkers and the list helpers) **3567 to 445 B (87.5%)**, `greet` 3527 to 645 B, `listid` 3723 to 555 B. The identity test is structural: an aggregate is rejected because it is internally a POINTER and canonically the DATA, and what remains must be an 8-byte 8-aligned canonical element whose generated per-element move is a bare `i64.store` of a bare `i64.load`. `List[Person]` keeps the loop in the regenerated golden, which is the check doing its job. A competent author sums the lengths once, allocates once, and does one `memory.copy` per part. Measured on `` `<<${a}|${b}|${a}|${b}>>` `` (9 parts): **58 fuel per argument byte, down to 42** with a k-ary concat alone, and to **6** with (a) as well (1024-byte arguments: 76377 to 20735 fuel). On a 3-part `greet` the fusion alone is worth little (21 to 20 fuel/byte), which is the point: the win is entirely in the arity, so fix this for the long templates, not for `` `Hello, ${x}` ``.     (e) **GROWTH ✅ FIXED 2026-09-02 (`fix/432e-wasm-heap-growth`); RECLAIM ✅ FIXED 2026-09-02 (`fix/432-wasm-reclaim`), see below.** `$alloc` now computes the end of the bump, refuses a round-to-8 or a bump that wraps i32, and calls a new `$__heap_grow` when the end crosses the current memory limit. `$__heap_grow` does its page arithmetic in pages (`end >>> 16` plus a ceiling bit, so nothing can overflow), grows by exactly the shortfall, and on `memory.grow` answering `-1` calls `$__heap_exhausted`. `cabi_realloc` is backed by the same `$alloc`, so the host's own placement of an incoming string grows the memory too and needed no change; `canonical.py` was not touched. **RE-BASELINED ON (a)/(c)/(f), because both audit numbers had moved and neither cliff had closed.** The audit's 40000-byte trap no longer reproduced: (a)'s zero-copy lift roughly doubled what one call can carry, so the single-call cliff was re-BISECTED rather than quoted, and sat at **65520 B ok, 65521 B refused**, with wasmtime's own canonical check (`realloc return: beyond end of memory`) in place of the pre-(a) `memory fault at wasm address 0x10000`. The sustained-call cliff moved the same way and no further: **64 calls with a 1 KiB string ok, 65 trapped** at `memory fault at wasm address 0x1020c` (the audit said 63; (a)/(c)/(f) shrank what a call allocates, they did not stop it accumulating). After this fix both are gone: 65521 B, 200000 B and 1000000 B arguments all round-trip, and 65536 calls with a 1 KiB string leave ONE instance alive with the heap at 67.6 MB. `bench/codegen/wasm/probe_heap.py` carries the re-bisected ladder. **What growth failure looks like.** There is no error channel out of `cabi_realloc` (the canonical ABI requires an allocator to return a usable pointer or not to return), so a capping host is answered with a deliberate trap at a NAMED site rather than an unchecked write. An operator sees `wasm trap: wasm 'unreachable' instruction executed` over a backtrace reading `__heap_exhausted` / `__heap_grow` / `alloc`, which says out of memory, instead of an address in a fault message, which says nothing. The two i32-wrap guards refuse at the same site, so a hostile `new_size` through `cabi_realloc` cannot buy a pointer with no bytes behind it. **RECLAIM ✅ FIXED 2026-09-02** (`fix/432-wasm-reclaim`, `backends/wasm/canonical.py`). Growth had converted "dies at call 65" into "grows without bound": the 65536-call run above was 67.6 MB of live memory for a workload whose working set is one 1 KiB string, and a component instance is long-lived by design (the component CLI re-instantiates per `--invoke`, which is exactly why this has to be measured on the core module). The fix is the **per-call arena** this item proposed, with ONE correction to the shape: the mark is NOT recorded on entry. The host places the arguments through `cabi_realloc` BEFORE the call, so an entry mark leaves the argument buffer — the larger half of what a call spends — above it and unreclaimed. The floor is instead the constant `$__hp` starts at (`$__canon_arena_base`), and every canonical export rewinds to it on the way out, so the arguments go with the scratch. RE-MEASURED through the REAL canonical export (`probe_heap.py` fact 3; facts 1 and 2 replay the per-call ALLOCATION and structurally cannot see a rewind that lives in the wrapper), `echo` with a 1 KiB argument, baseline before vs after: **1040 to 8 B after 1 call, 66056 to 8 after 64, 1056776 to 8 after 1024, 67633160 to 8 after 65536**, and `memory.size` **1033 pages to 1** across the same 65536 calls. FLAT, which is what this item asked for. Fuel cost: **ZERO**, re-bisected either side — `echo` 67 at 16 B, 256 B and 4 KiB alike, `greet` 16645/17125, `ids` 136 at n=4 and 8296 at n=1024, `dbl` 11, every one of them unmoved — because wasmtime charges no fuel for a `global.get`/`global.set`. Size cost: **+29 B** core.wasm (`echo` 3669 to 3698, `greet` 3713 to 3742, `listid` 3801 to 3830). SOUNDNESS IS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED. A rewind is only correct for a module that parks nothing in the heap across calls, and `canonical._arena_safe` reads that off the emitted module: a live-across-calls heap value has to be reachable from a module-level cell, this tier's only such cell is a global, immutable globals are const-initialised (the return area and the literal segments, both BELOW the floor), i64 globals hold `Int` values rather than addresses, and a mutable i32 global cannot be holding an address if every write to it stores an `i32.const`. The activation cursors (`$__step`, `$__dstep`) and the commit flag pass that test; a module-level binding of a compound and the witnessed-accumulator head `$__mw_head` do not, and those modules keep the old never-reclaim heap rather than getting a wrong one. A `(start ...)` function is refused for the same reason. ORDERING: the rewind is a POINTER move and never a write, and it is the last statement before the wrapper's tail, so the result the host has yet to lift is still in memory; the first byte that can overwrite it belongs to the NEXT call, which a single-threaded instance cannot start before the host has finished lifting this one. Regression: `backends/wasm/test_heap_reclaim_432e.py` (12 tests: four on the `_arena_safe` verdict including both refusals, four on the emitted shape, four executed — the flat `$__hp`, the one-page high-water mark over 65536 calls, a 200000-byte single call still growing and still answering, and repeated round-trips at five lengths, since a rewind hands the same addresses out call after call and a stale read would surface as a WRONG ANSWER rather than a trap). Goldens: the three that carry the boundary (`canonical_echoer`, `canonical_aggregates`, `canonical_service` `.core.wat`); `functions.wat` did not move, the change being entirely in `canonical.py`. SELF-HOST: no port — `cabi_realloc`, `__canon_*` and `$__canon_arena_base` occur ZERO times anywhere under `selfhost/`. Regression: `backends/wasm/test_heap_growth_432e.py` (7 tests: both re-bisected proofs plus both refusal paths). Self-host: ported, `selfhost/emit_wasm.rvl` `helper_preamble()` embeds the preamble verbatim and now carries the identical bytes (checked directly against `_helper_funcs()`, 20365 B either side, not only through the oracle). Goldens moved by the same 34-added/6-removed hunk in all four (`functions.wat`, `canonical_echoer/aggregates/service.core.wat`): the two new functions ahead of `$alloc`, and `$alloc`'s body. `Beacon.wat`, `Auditor.wat` and `Pulse.wat` regenerated byte-identical (they carry no memory preamble). ORIGINAL FINDING: **the emitted heap is one fixed 64 KiB page that never grows and never frees, so a long-lived instance dies.** `emit.py:1938` and `emit.py:5138` emit `(memory (export "memory") 1)`, `$alloc` (`emit.py:2773`) only bumps `$__hp`, and neither it nor the exported `cabi_realloc` ever calls `memory.grow` (`grep -c memory.grow` over `emit.py` and `canonical.py` is 0). Two executed proofs in `bench/codegen/wasm/probe_heap.py`: a single `echo` call with a **40000-byte** `Str` traps with `memory fault at wasm address 0x10000 in linear memory of size 0x10000`, the host's own write of the argument already being out of bounds; and replaying the per-call allocation on the core module, **63 calls with a 1 KiB string exhaust the instance** (32 calls leave the heap at 33280 of 65536 B, 64 traps). This is a correctness cliff as much as a perf one, and it is the reason it is ranked here rather than last. FIX: `memory.grow` in `$alloc` and in `cabi_realloc` when the bump would cross the current limit, which is a bounded change; reclaiming per-call scratch is the larger follow-on and (a) plus (c) remove most of what would need reclaiming.
    (f) **The 8-byte canonical return area is bump-allocated on every call although it is constant for the module.** `canonical.py:640` emits `(local.set $area (call $alloc (i32.const N)))` per canonical export. The component host reads the return area before it can re-enter the instance, so one module-level cell serves every call on a single-threaded instance. Measured: **13 fuel per call**, constant, plus 8 bytes of otherwise unbounded heap growth per call removed, which compounds with (e). Small on its own; free to take alongside (e). **FIXED 2026-09-02** (same commit). One `$__canon_ret_area` global, sized to the widest result any export in the module returns and carved off the bottom of the bump heap so it can never be handed out again. RE-MEASURED 13 fuel per call on `echo` (58 for the lift alone, 45 with the area, 49 with the item-432(a) bounds check), and the 8 bytes per call of unreclaimed heap growth are gone. `scalar` stays at 11 fuel, confirming NEGATIVE RESULT (1): a direct-returned `Int` never touched a return area.
    (g) **No constant folding: `7 * 6` emits two `i64.const` and a `call $int_mul` with its overflow test.** `emit.py:2207` routes every `+ - *` through the checked helper regardless of whether both operands are literals the emitter can evaluate. Measured on `fn scaled(n: Int) -> Int { return n * 1000 + 7 * 6 }`: **47 fuel down to 29** when the constant multiply is folded, so **18 fuel per folded checked op**. Lowest expected win in this item and listed for completeness; **FIXED 2026-09-03** (`fix/113-wasm-perf-remainder`, PR #259, `backends/wasm/emit.py` `_fold_int_const`, applied in `_bin_expr` and in `_un_expr`'s subtract-from-zero). RE-MEASURED on the committed harness with a new `programs/constfold.revl` and a `const_fold` variant: **47 to 29 fuel**, exactly the audit's **18 fuel per folded checked op**, and the variant is now a no-op against the fixed emitter. The operands are matched as EMITTED WAT rather than as IR nodes, which makes the fold compositional for nothing: `2 * 3 * 4 + 5 - 6` collapses to one `(i64.const 23)`, and `-5` folds through the unary subtract-from-zero. **The proposed OVERFLOW SHAPE was measured and REJECTED.** This item proposed making an overflowing constant expression a compile-time refusal. That would make the wasm tier alone refuse a program every other tier compiles and traps in at run time, and `docs/arithmetic.md` pins the TRAP; so an overflowing fold is DECLINED instead and the checked helper stays, keeping the trap exactly where it was. `9223372036854775807 + 1` still emits two constants and `(call $int_add)`; `4611686018427387904 * (0 - 2)`, which is exactly `Int.MIN` and therefore representable, folds. `/` and `%` are not folded: they are single native instructions whose zero-divisor and `MIN / -1` traps this tier deliberately leaves to wasm. SELF-HOST: PORTED (`selfhost/emit_wasm.rvl` `fold_const`, whose overflow guards are written so the CHECK itself cannot overflow — this tier's `+ - *` trap, so the fold cannot be decided by computing the answer first), and `tests/fixtures/emit_wasm_corpus/constfold.rvl` puts the folds, the declined overflows and the exact-`Int.MIN` product under the byte-agreement oracle rather than trusting a corpus that never contained a constant expression (the item-429 trap).

(3) The checked-arithmetic helpers `$int_add`/`$int_sub`/`$int_mul` are the branch-free shapes an author would write, and cost nothing beyond the fold in (g). (4) `$__canon_lower_str` is already zero-copy: it writes a pointer and a length and copies nothing. (6) The record lift/lower helpers do one copy per field with no redundant round trip. Numbers below are the minimum over 15 samples after warmup on openjdk 26.0.2, emitted-vs-hand-written, N as each case's `Drive` declares it. Timings were also not taken for a second, independent reason: the audit machine was running about a dozen other agents, and on the JVM machine load distorts JIT compilation as well as wall clock, so an interleaved A/B ratio would not have cancelled it either. The deliverable is therefore a static audit plus a runnable harness, `bench/codegen/java/`, which reports ALLOCATED BYTES PER OP (a count, unaffected by load) and compiled class-file sizes, and deliberately reports no duration at all. Six cases, each an emitted program paired with the Java a competent Java developer writes for the same semantics, with a `setup()` that asserts the two sides agree before anything is sampled. `run.py --static` needs no JDK; the default mode exits 77 when none is present.

For a provide method whose body is the template literal `[req] $<msg> #<n> end` (written with the usual backtick/dollar-brace spelling), emit produces `return String.format("[req] %s #%s end", msg, n);`. Hand-written: `return "[req] " + msg + " #" + n + " end";`. THE FIX: each record class and each case class now carries a generated `equals`/`hashCode`. A primitive component (long/int/double/boolean) compares with the primitive `==`, never `Double.compare` or `Double.equals`, which are the same `doubleToLongBits` trap R2 was; a reference component routes through `revlEq`, so a nested record recurses into the inner class's own generated `equals` and a Float inside a List/Map/Opt keeps the IEEE rule.
