Both helpers keep the `_uses_equality` gating idiom, emitted exactly where they are called, so a record of nothing but Int/Float/Bool emits byte-identically to before and `backends/java/golden/user_cache.java` does not move at all. NaN DECISION, STATED BECAUSE IT HAS A COST: there is deliberately no `if (this == o) return true` fast path, so the answer never depends on aliasing, which matches rust's derived `PartialEq`. IEEE equality is not an equivalence relation, so a value carrying a NaN is not equal to itself and does not satisfy `Object.equals`'s reflexivity requirement; such a value is therefore not a well-behaved hash key on this tier. `HashMap`/`HashSet` short-circuit on `key == k`, so a lookup with the identical reference still finds it, but a structurally identical NaN-carrying lookup never will, and `List.contains`/`indexOf`/`Set.remove` can miss. Matching every other tier is the requirement and this is what it costs on a host whose collections assume an equivalence relation. **EVIDENCE: EXECUTED ON A REAL JVM, and this item's own header is wrong about that.** There IS a working JDK on this machine, openjdk 26.0.2 at `/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk/bin`. It is keg-only, so it is not on PATH, and the `/usr/bin/java` macOS stub that IS on PATH errors with "Unable to locate a Java Runtime" while still satisfying `shutil.which("java")`. That stub is what produced this item's "NO JDK ON THE AUDIT MACHINE" header and R1/R2/R3's inspection-only labels; the perf findings F1-F10 genuinely were static, but the correctness claims did not have to be. With `PATH=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk/bin:$PATH` the divergence was REPRODUCED AND FIXED BY EXECUTION: the pre-fix emitter fails `PROBES["structural equality"]` on the JVM with `java.lang.AssertionError` at `testRecordsCompareByValue`, and the post-fix emitter passes it, along with the new `PROBES["declared value types compare structurally"]` and the riders' `PROBES["true division and IEEE float equality"]`. `pytest tests/test_cross_tier_execution.py -k java` with `REVL_CROSS_TIER_SLOW=1` is 33 passed, 0 skipped, and `test_emitted_code_survives_its_toolchain[java]` runs green. The same probe runs green on python, go and typescript. THE NaN CONSEQUENCE WAS MEASURED, NOT ARGUED: `x.equals(x)` is FALSE for a NaN-carrying record, so reflexivity is gone; `HashMap.get` still finds it by the identical reference (HashMap short-circuits on `key == k`) but returns null for a structurally identical key; `HashSet` will hold two "equal" NaN values at once; and `ArrayList.contains`, which has no such short-circuit, returns FALSE for a value that is literally in the list. Every non-NaN value round-trips correctly, including a distinct-but-equal nested record and a -0.0/0.0 pair at the top level and inside a List, which is `revlHash` doing its job. GUARD: four new STATIC guards that need no toolchain and run in the `frontend` job, verified to FAIL against the pre-fix emitter and pass after: `test_java_declared_value_types_carry_a_structural_equals` sweeps every emitted value class rather than naming one, so a future third shape cannot opt out; plus the Float IEEE, nested-record and nullary-case guards. SELF-HOST: ported to `selfhost/emit_java.rvl` per item 429's standing rule, checked in the source, and the byte-equality corpus agrees again on `records.rvl`, `adts.rvl` and `comp_host_map_generic.rvl`. STEP (d) ABOVE IS NOW UNBLOCKED: this was the gap that made exporting `REVL_CROSS_TIER_SLOW=1` in the `conformance` job turn red. **STILL OPEN, one level further out, and EXECUTED so the next agent does not have to re-derive it:** `revlEq` compares `Bytes` (`byte[]`) with `Objects.equals`, which is ARRAY IDENTITY. Compiled and run on openjdk 26.0.2, `beq(x, y)` for two equal but distinct `byte[]{1,2,3}` is FALSE and `beq(x, x)` is true, where python's `bytes` compare structurally (`bytes([1,2,3]) == bytes([1,2,3])` is True) and rust's `Vec<u8>` does the same. A record with a `Bytes` component inherits the hole uniformly (`blob(x).equals(blob(y))` is likewise false), which is exactly why it was left alone here instead of being widened into this fix: one hole reported once beats a record that compares Bytes differently from top-level `==`. Reachability is currently narrow, since no literal or builtin produces a `Bytes` value and it can only enter through an extern signature, which is presumably how it went unnoticed. It wants its own item: a `byte[]` arm in `revlEq` (`java.util.Arrays.equals`) and in `revlHash` (`java.util.Arrays.hashCode`), plus a cross-tier probe, which needs a per-tier extern body to construct the value.
    **NEGATIVE RESULTS, examined and FINE.** The modern component path (`_emit_component_modern`) emits close to what a Java developer writes: final fields, constructor injection, one `ctx.get` per required key hoisted out of the provider, no per-call resolution, no defensive copies, and `fx.track(Disposables.of(() -> ...))` per effect, which is one capturing lambda for an inverse that genuinely must capture. `Math.addExact`/`subtractExact`/`multiplyExact` are the correct lowering of trapping `Int` arithmetic per `docs/arithmetic.md` and are HotSpot intrinsics, so the hand-written equivalent is the same code. `?? ` lowering to `orElseGet(() -> ...)` allocates nothing per call, because a non-capturing lambda is cached by `LambdaMetafactory`; `orElse` would be marginally cheaper for a literal right operand but the laziness the comment cites is real for a non-literal one, so this is not worth a special case. `revlMapKeys`'s comparator is a non-capturing lambda, so hoisting it buys nothing, and its sort is load-bearing for canonical `Str` order past U+FFFF; only the trailing `List.copyOf` of a list no caller holds is removable, two objects and one O(k) copy per call, which is bench case `map_keys` and ranks below F6. `revlSlice`'s `List.copyOf(xs.subList(..))` is what a competent developer writes, since returning the view would retain the parent list. The host `Map` runtime is a `ConcurrentHashMap` with O(1) insert/get/remove and an atomic `putIfAbsent`, correct and appropriately typed. The `RevlFrame` teardown runtime allocates one capturing lambda per registered inverse, which is unavoidable, and its `ExecutorService` is created lazily and only on an abort that has compensations, so it costs nothing on the clean path. `Pool` is O(n) on release with a sort, but it is a deterministic in-memory simulation with pool sizes in single digits and no hot path, so it is not worth touching. Emitted `if`/`while`/`for` control flow, `List.of` for list literals, record and sealed-interface emission, and the `switch` pattern lowering for `match` are all what a Java developer writes.
    **HYPOTHESES, RESOLVED 2026-09-02 on `fix/433-java-codegen-perf`.** All three are now settled by execution, and the settling changed two answers. F6's class-file cost was a hypothesis ("presumably costs class-file bytes in proportion to source bytes") and is now MEASURED with javac: the proportion holds and is if anything understated — 42 to 66 percent of the compiled unit on the three files the audit named. F1's object count for `String.format`, read off the `Formatter` source rather than measured, was CONSERVATIVE: the real gap is 508968 against 40040 allocated bytes per op. The blanket claim that "every allocation figure in this item is a static count of construction sites" is exactly what made F5 wrong, because construction SITES are not BYTES: F5's ten-sites-against-three became 221224 bytes against 286760, in the emitter's favour. `bench/codegen/java/run.py` did replace all ten with `getCurrentThreadAllocatedBytes` deltas, as it was written to. Relates to 397 (the host-Map thread-safety fix whose reasoning F3's rider extends), 391 (the standing self-host port question, which F1, F2, F3, F5 and F6 each raise for `selfhost/emit_java.rvl`), and 327 (per-backend drift, which R1 is an instance of).

434. PARTIALLY LANDED 2026-09-02, now ON MAIN (`0a8068ed`, `07e221b0`; branch `fix/434-go-codegen-perf` deleted after landing, verified ancestor of main), REMAINDER LANDED 2026-09-02 via `fix/434-go-codegen-perf-remainder` (merged `7d2aa8b7`, branch deleted): (c) stage two and (g); (d) remains the only open finding, deferred to its own slice because it changes the Opt/Result encoding the whole v3 tier is written against: (h), (f), (c) stage one, the self-rebind analysis (a)+(b), and (e) are done and measured; (c) stage two and (g) are done and measured on the remainder branch; (d) is the only finding still open, see the two **WHAT LANDED** paragraphs at the end of this item. **GO CODEGEN PERFORMANCE AUDIT: SEVEN STDLIB LOWERINGS ARE QUADRATIC OR ALLOCATING WHERE THE HAND-WRITTEN GO IS NEITHER (2026-09-02).** Audit of the code `backends/go/emit.py` GENERATES, measured against the Go a competent Go developer writes for the same semantics. Harness committed at `bench/codegen/go/` as real `testing.B` benchmarks (`go test ./ab/ -bench . -benchmem -benchtime=2000x -run XXX`), with `Test*` functions that fail if the hand-written side stops being the same program, and `regen.sh` to re-emit after an emitter change. The emitter was NOT edited. **No timings were taken and none should be quoted from this item**: the audit machine was carrying about a dozen concurrent agents, so every figure below is load-independent by construction. The evidence is `allocs/op` and `B/op` from `go test -benchmem` (exact and reproducible), `go build -gcflags='-m'` escape analysis, static counts, and complexity arguments. Toolchain: **Go 1.26.5 darwin/arm64**, matching the `actions/setup-go` pin in CI. **stc-go was not resolved and is not needed**: the ir_version 3 pure tier the probes exercise is ordinary Go with no runtime dependency, so the harness runs offline.

    Two structural facts set the blast radius for everything below. First, the component (v1/v2) tier and the pure v3 tier share the SAME stdlib helper preamble and route to it from two dispatchers (`emit.py:1040`ff and `emit.py:4086`ff), so a single helper fix moves both tiers at once. Second, `selfhost/emit_go.rvl` itself scans source with `s.charCodeAt(a)` inside `while` loops (lines 367, 369), so the self-hosted Go emitter, compiled to Go, inherits finding (c) on its own hot path.

    (a) **✅ DONE 2026-09-02 (`0a8068ed`, `fix/434-go-codegen-perf`).** **`List.push` in a loop is quadratic: one full copy of the list per element.** `revlListPush` (`emit.py:6194`) does `make([]T, 0, len(xs)+1)` then two appends, which is the correct lowering for a persistent push and the wrong one for `out = out.push(x)`, where the previous list is dead on the next line. Executed, `BenchmarkCollect*`: emitted **100 allocs / 42,225 B** at N=100 and **1001 allocs / 4,274,103 B** at N=1000, so a 10x input costs 101x the bytes. Hand-written `append`: **1 alloc / 896 B** and **1 alloc / 8,192 B**. Escape analysis names the site: `make([]go.shape.int64, 0, len(xs) + 1) escapes to heap` and two `append escapes to heap` per call. FIX: when a `var` binding is rebound from its own `push` and is not otherwise live at that point, emit `out = append(out, x)`. A conservative same-statement self-rebind check covers the whole idiom. Blast radius: both tiers; goldens regenerate through `backends/go/regen.sh`; no self-host port needed yet (`emit_go.rvl` emits only the overflow/overflow32/fdiv preambles, not the stdlib one). **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** landed through the shared self-rebind analysis, not a special case; measured numbers in WHAT LANDED below.

    (b) **✅ DONE 2026-09-02 (`0a8068ed`, `fix/434-go-codegen-perf`).** **`Map.set` in a loop is quadratic: the whole map is copied per insertion.** `revlMapSet` (`emit.py:5964`) allocates a fresh `map[K]V` and copies every entry. Same persistence argument, same dead-previous-value fact. Executed, `BenchmarkTally*` over 100 and 1000 distinct keys: emitted **384 allocs / 227,433 B** and **3990 allocs / 19,168,881 B**, so a 10x input costs 84x the bytes; hand-written in-place `m[k] = v` gives **3 allocs / 3,496 B** and **5 allocs / 54,609 B**. FIX: the same self-rebind rule as (a), emitting `m[k] = v`. `remove` (`emit.py:5985`) has the identical shape and should move with it. Blast radius as (a). **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** same shared analysis as (a); measured numbers in WHAT LANDED below.

    (c) **✅ DONE: STAGE ONE 2026-09-02 (`0a8068ed`), STAGE TWO 2026-09-02 (`fix/434-go-codegen-perf-remainder`).** **Every `Str` code-point read materializes the whole string as `[]rune`.** `revlStrCharCodeAt` and `revlStrCharAt` (`emit.py:6154`, `6159`) are two lines each and both begin `r := []rune(s)`. `charAt`, `charCodeAt` and `codepoint_at` (item 276) all route there, from both dispatchers. That makes a scan loop quadratic in TIME and in BYTES. Executed, `BenchmarkScan*` (sum the code points of a string): emitted **78 allocs / 24,963 B** for a 78-code-point string and **781 allocs / 2,496,127 B** for a 780-code-point one, exactly one whole-string rune copy per character; hand-written `for _, r := range s` is **0 allocs / 0 B at both sizes**. A single read is not free either: `BenchmarkCharCodeAt` is **1 alloc / 320 B** emitted against **0 / 0** hand-written, and the 320 B tracks the length of the string, not the index requested. Escape analysis: `string(r[i]) escapes to heap` at the `charAt` site. FIX, in two stages. The cheap one, all inside the helper, is to walk with `utf8.DecodeRuneInString` instead of materializing: still O(i), but 0 allocations, and it alone takes the scan benchmark from 781 allocations to 0. The real one is to recognize the scan shape (an index that starts at 0, advances by 1 and is bounded by `s.length()`) and emit `for i, r := range s`. Stage one is small and unlocks most of the win; stage two needs a loop-shape pattern in the statement lowering. Blast radius as (a), plus: `selfhost/lexer.rvl` and `selfhost/emit_go.rvl` are the programs this hurts most. **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** `revlStrCharAt`/`revlStrCharCodeAt` walk with `utf8.DecodeRuneInString` (`backends/go/emit.py:6545`, `:6557`, `:6576`); the rest of the `[]rune`-materializing surface is stage two and is untouched (`[]rune(` still appears at `:6482`, `:6500-6501`, `:6527`). **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02 (remainder):** stage two landed as `_v3_scan_loops` in `backends/go/emit.py`, narrower than the audit's sketch and measured in the second WHAT LANDED paragraph below.

    (d) **❌ NOT DONE, AS THE AUDIT ORDERED, RE-VERIFIED ON `bd0f4d19`.** **`Opt[T]` is a sealed interface in the v3 tier, so every Opt that leaves a function heap-boxes.** `RevlOpt[T] interface{ isRevlOpt() }` with `RevlSome[T] struct{ Value T }` (`emit.py:5884`) means a non-pointer payload must be boxed to satisfy the interface. Executed: `BenchmarkMaybe` (an `Opt[Int]` returned across a function boundary) is **1 alloc / 8 B** emitted against **0 / 0** for the two-value `(int64, bool)` form; `BenchmarkBoxedList` (200 lookups collected into a `List[Opt[Int]]`) is **400 allocs / 344,332 B** against **1 alloc / 3,200 B**, which is exactly two allocations per element, one box plus one (a)-style push copy. Escape analysis names both arms: `RevlSome[go.shape.int64]{...} escapes to heap` and `RevlNone[go.shape.int64]{} escapes to heap`. Note the benchmark deliberately uses map values above 255, because Go's `runtime.staticuint64s` table makes small boxed integers free and hides the whole finding. FIX: lower `Opt[T]` to `struct { Value T; Ok bool }` on the v3 tier, the same two-value shape the v1/v2 return position already uses (`(T, bool)` in the backend contract table). This is the largest single change proposed here and it moves every `Opt`-shaped golden, so it wants its own slice. `Result[T, E]` has the identical encoding and the same argument applies. **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** `RevlOpt` is still a sealed interface in `backends/go/emit.py`. Read it with the negative result below (a non-escaping `Opt` costs nothing), which is what makes this narrower than it looks.

    (e) **✅ DONE 2026-09-02 (`0a8068ed`, `fix/434-go-codegen-perf`).** **String `+` in a loop is quadratic, and no `strings.Builder` is ever emitted.** `out = out + x + sep` lowers to `((out + x) + sep)` verbatim (`emit.py:6133` for the `concat` builtin, plain `+` for the operator). Executed, `BenchmarkBuild*`: emitted **100 allocs / 37,009 B** at N=100 and **1001 allocs / 3,717,392 B** at N=1000, a 100x byte growth for a 10x input; a `strings.Builder` with one `Grow` is **1 alloc / 704 B** and **1 alloc / 8,192 B**. Escape analysis: `out + x + sep escapes to heap`. FIX: recognize `s = s + e` (and `s = s.concat(e)`) as the accumulator of a loop and emit a `strings.Builder` for the loop's extent, with a `Grow` where the bound is known. Same self-rebind analysis as (a) and (b), so all three fixes share one piece of machinery, which is a good reason to do them together. **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** landed through its OWN machinery, not (a)/(b)'s; see WHAT LANDED below.

    (f) **✅ DONE 2026-09-02 (`0a8068ed`, `fix/434-go-codegen-perf`).** **Interpolation and `Int.to_str` go through `fmt.Sprintf("%v", ...)` even though the operand types are known at emit time.** `_go_v3_interp` (`emit.py:4192`) already calls `_go_v3_infer_type` and already special-cases `Float`, then falls through to `%v` for everything else; `to_str` is a literal `fmt.Sprintf("%d", x)` on both tiers (`emit.py:1088` and `4125`); `_format` (`emit.py:1160`) emits `%v` unconditionally. `%v` takes `...any`, which boxes each operand. This finding carries an **in-language control**, the strongest evidence in the audit: `` `${a}/${b}` `` and `a + "/" + b` are the same value over the same two `Str` operands, and the SAME emitter produces **3 allocs / 48 B** for the first and **1 alloc / 16 B** for the second. The hand-written concatenation is also 1 alloc / 16 B. A `Str`+`Int` interpolation is **3 allocs / 48 B** against **1 alloc / 24 B**, and `Int.to_str` is **2 allocs / 16 B** against `strconv.FormatInt`'s **1 alloc / 4 B**. Escape analysis pins the two extra allocations precisely: on the `Sprintf` line, `... argument does not escape` (the varargs slice is stack-allocated) while `name escapes to heap` and `n escapes to heap` (the two boxed operands are not). FIX: in `_go_v3_interp` and `_format`, use the type already inferred. All-`Str` parts concatenate with `+` and need no `fmt` import at all; an `Int` part uses `strconv.FormatInt`; `%v` stays only as the fallback for a type that could not be inferred. `to_str` becomes `strconv.FormatInt(x, 10)`. **This is the one finding that needs a self-host port**: `selfhost/emit_go.rvl` carries the same interp lowering at lines 708 to 731, `tests/fixtures/emit_go_corpus/strings.rvl` exercises it, and `tests/test_selfhost_emit_go.py` is a byte-agreement oracle, so the reference and the self-host must move together or the new shape goes behind a new IR key. **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** no `Sprintf("%v"` remains in `backends/go/emit.py`.

    (g) **✅ DONE 2026-09-02 (`fix/434-go-codegen-perf-remainder`).** **`Str.indexOf` and `Str.slice` allocate the whole string as `[]rune` to answer a question that needs no copy.** `revlStrIndexOf` (`emit.py:6109`) converts BOTH operands and then runs a naive O(n*m) scan; `revlStrSlice` (`emit.py:6091`) converts and re-materializes. Executed: `BenchmarkIndexOf` is **1 alloc / 320 B** emitted against **0 / 0** hand-written, and `BenchmarkTake` is **2 allocs / 328 B** against **0 / 0**. Escape analysis: `string(r[a:b]) escapes to heap`. FIX: `indexOf` is `strings.Index` plus one `utf8.RuneCountInString` over the matched prefix, which gives the same code-point index with no allocation and drops the search from O(n*m) to the standard library's; `slice` is a byte-offset walk returning a substring, which in Go shares the backing array and allocates nothing. `revlStrSplit`'s empty-separator branch (`emit.py:6157`ff) has the same `[]rune` materialization and can move with it. **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** `revlStrIndexOf` (`backends/go/emit.py:6499`) still does `rs := []rune(s)` and `rn := []rune(sub)`. **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02 (remainder):** `revlStrIndexOf` is `strings.Index` plus one `utf8.RuneCountInString`, `revlStrSlice` is a byte walk returning a substring, and `revlStrSplit`'s empty-separator branch hands out substrings; the `[]rune` forms survive only as the invalid-UTF-8 fallbacks. Measured in the second WHAT LANDED paragraph below.

    (h) **✅ DONE 2026-09-02 (`0a8068ed`, `fix/434-go-codegen-perf`).** **`Map.keys()` sorts with an insertion sort, which is quadratic on anything but a small map.** `revlMapKeys` (`emit.py:5998`) carries a hand-rolled insertion sort with the comment "symbol-table keys come in small sets". That premise does not hold: `Map.keys()` IS the iteration surface for `Map` (docs/stdlib-2.0.md), so it is on the path of every map traversal a program does. **This finding has no allocation evidence and is a complexity argument, stated as such**: `BenchmarkKeys*` reports **1 alloc / 1,152 B** at n=64 and **1 alloc / 10,880 B** at n=1024 on BOTH sides, identical, because the allocation is just the key slice. The gap is O(n^2) comparisons against O(n log n). FIX: `slices.Sort(keys)`. Go's `string <` is UTF-8 byte lexicographic, exactly the canonical order the current sort produces, so the emitted order is unchanged and the goldens stay byte-identical apart from the helper body. `slices` is standard library, and the existing comment's stated reason for the hand-rolled sort (avoiding a `sort` import) is satisfied by the import block the emitter already builds conditionally. **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** `revlMapKeys` (`backends/go/emit.py:6392-6399`) sorts with `slices.Sort`, and so does the host runtime's `Map.Keys`.

    **NEGATIVE RESULTS, deliberately recorded so nobody re-audits them.** All executed, all in the committed harness as controls.
    - `for (x of xs)` over a `List[Int]` with an accumulator lowers to a plain `range` loop: **0 allocs/op on both sides**. The emitter's `_ = x` blank-assign after each binding costs nothing.
    - A statement-position `if`/`else if` chain lowers flat, with no wrapper: **0 allocs/op both sides**.
    - **The match lowering is fine, despite looking exactly like a per-call closure allocation.** Every `match` (and every expression-position `if`) is emitted as an immediately-invoked `func() T { ... }()`. It reads like a closure allocated per call and it is not: **0 allocs/op on both sides**, and `-gcflags='-m'` reports the literal inlined. Do not "fix" this.
    - **An `Opt` that does not escape costs nothing, so finding (d) is narrower than it looks.** `BenchmarkFind`, where a `Map.lookup` is consumed by a `match` in the same function, is **0 allocs/op on both sides**: Go's escape analysis plus inlining keeps `RevlSome` on the stack. (d) bites only when the `Opt` crosses a function boundary or lands in a collection.
    - **No `append`-without-capacity site exists in the emitted preamble.** Every `make` in `revlListConcat`, `revlListSlice`, `revlMapKeys` and `revlStrSplit` carries a capacity hint. `revlListConcat` and `revlListSlice` are single-allocation and correct as written.
    - No per-call closure allocation was found anywhere in the v3 tier, and no defensive slice copy beyond the ones the persistent-value semantics actually require.

    **BLAST RADIUS, measured.** 14 checked-in emitted Go files carry the helpers touched by (a) through (e), (g) and (h); 15 carry `fmt.Sprintf` and are touched by (f). All regenerate through `backends/go/regen.sh`. `backends/go/test_emit_go.py` carries 4 `Sprintf` assertions and 3 helper assertions. The executed scenario suites under `backends/go/scenarios/` and `backends/go/v3/` are the real gate: they RUN on stc-go, so a wrong lowering fails rather than diffing. Only (f) needs the `selfhost/emit_go.rvl` port today.

    **SUGGESTED ORDER.** (h) and (f) first, since both are contained and (h) changes no emitted bytes outside one helper. Then (c) stage one, which is two lines of helper for the largest measured allocation reduction in the audit. Then the shared self-rebind analysis that (a), (b) and (e) all want. (d) last and on its own, since it changes the `Opt` and `Result` encodings the whole v3 tier is written against.


    **WHAT LANDED (2026-09-02, `fix/434-go-codegen-perf`).** Numbers are `allocs/op` / `B/op` from the committed harness at the same `-benchtime=2000x`, emitted before to emitted after, with the hand-written yardstick in parentheses. No timings, for the reason the audit gives.
    - **(h) DONE.** `revlMapKeys` and the host runtime's `Map.Keys` both sort with `slices.Sort` now. `Map.Keys` in `_host_runtime()` is a SECOND site the audit did not name, carrying the same hand-rolled insertion sort. As the audit predicted this moves no allocation counter: `BenchmarkKeys*` is 1 alloc / 1,152 B at n=64 and 1 / 10,880 at n=1024 on both sides, before and after. The change is O(n log n) comparisons for O(n^2), and the order is unchanged because Go's `string <` is what both sorts use; `TestHandMatchesEmittedValues` compares the emitted key order against the hand one and stays green. `slices` is imported unconditionally on the component tiers (the host runtime is unconditional there) and on `used_map` for the pure tier.
    - **(f) DONE, and it closes the audit's in-language control.** `_go_v3_interp`, `_format` and `Int.to_str` on both tiers now render from the operand types the emitter already had: all-`Str` parts concatenate with `+`, an `Int`/`Int32` part goes through `strconv.FormatInt` and a `Bool` part through `strconv.FormatBool`, and `%v` through `fmt.Sprintf` stays only as the fallback for a part whose type could not be inferred. `BenchmarkTagEmitted` (`${a}/${b}`) 3 / 48 to **1 / 16**, exactly `BenchmarkTagJoinedEmitted` and `BenchmarkTagHand`. `BenchmarkRenderEmitted` (`Int.to_str`) 2 / 16 to **1 / 4**, exactly the hand `strconv.FormatInt`. `BenchmarkLabelEmitted` (`Str` plus `Int`) 3 / 48 to **2 / 28** against the hand form's 1 / 24; the residual allocation is `FormatInt`'s own string, which only a `strings.Builder` lowering would fold away, and that is left undone. A module whose only `fmt` use was interpolation now emits no `fmt` import at all (`backends/go/v3/stdlib/gen.go` is the visible case). One defect this surfaced and fixed: the ir_version 1/2 tier lowers revl `Int` to Go `int`, which `strconv.FormatInt` refuses, so the component tier widens with `int64(..)`. Caught by `tests/test_conformance_validate.py::test_emitted_code_survives_its_toolchain[go]`, which compiles the emitted code.
    - **ONE RIDER, found by landing (f) and fixed with it.** `_go_v3_infer_type` returned a flat `"Int"` for every `-`, `*` and `%` bin node, ignoring the `operands` type the checker had already resolved onto the node, and nothing downstream could tell that `"Int"` from a real one. Harmless while interpolation only special-cased `Float` and sent everything else through `%v`; the moment interpolation rendered FROM the inferred type, `${(0.0 - 1.0) * 0.0}` reached `strconv.FormatInt` on a float64, which does not compile. Caught by `tests/test_cross_tier_execution.py::test_float_interpolation_is_canonical[go-negative zero loses its sign in text]`, which BUILDS and RUNS the emitted Go rather than diffing it. The fix honours the annotation the node already carries. No checked-in golden moved.

    - **(c) STAGE ONE DONE.** `revlStrCharAt` and `revlStrCharCodeAt` walk with `utf8.DecodeRuneInString` instead of `[]rune(s)`, and `charAt` returns the substring, which shares the receiver's bytes. `BenchmarkScanEmitted78` 78 / 24,961 to **0 / 0**; `BenchmarkScanEmitted780` 780 / 2,496,095 to **0 / 0**, matching the hand `for _, r := range s` exactly at both sizes; `BenchmarkCharCodeAtEmitted` 1 / 320 to **0 / 0**. Stage two (recognising the scan shape and emitting `for i, r := range s`) is NOT done: the walk is still O(i) per read, so a scan is still quadratic in TIME, just no longer in bytes. An out-of-range index falls through to the `[]rune(s)[i]` it always was, so it panics identically. Verified against `[]rune` over 4,011 strings (astral, invalid UTF-8, random bytes) at every index from -3 to n+2 including panic behaviour: zero divergence. The `astralText` and `invalidText` fixtures plus `TestCharCodeAtIsRuneIndexed` are now in the harness so this stays pinned.
    - **(a) and (b) DONE, through the shared analysis the audit asked for, not through special cases.** `_v3_self_rebind_locals` (`backends/go/emit.py`) decides UNIQUE OWNERSHIP over a whole function body. A name qualifies when every write to it is either a fresh allocation this function made (a list literal or `Map.empty()`) or a self-rebind through `push`/`set`/`remove`, with at least one of each, AND every other occurrence is a read that retains no reference: the receiver of a read-only builtin, an index target, a `for ... of` iterable, or the returned expression. Anything else disqualifies it, including being bound to a second name, passed as an argument, or stored into another collection. The rule closes over calls: a caller binds a returned list with a `let` whose value is a CALL, not a fresh literal, so no caller binding ever qualifies and no alias can observe an in-place write. A qualifying rebind emits `out = append(out, x)`, `m[k] = v` or `delete(m, k)`. `BenchmarkCollectEmitted100` 100 / 42,224 to **8 / 2,040** and `Collect1000` 1000 / 4,273,989 to **12 / 25,208**, against a hand 1 / 8,192 that pre-sizes with `make`, so `append`'s geometric growth is the whole remaining gap and it is linear. `BenchmarkTallyEmitted100` 384 / 227,435 to **9 / 6,696** and `Tally1000` 3,989 / 19,168,855 to **15 / 54,153** against the hand form's 5 / 54,610. `BenchmarkBoxedListEmitted` 400 / 344,335 to **209 / 10,928**: the (a)-style push copy is gone and the 200 remaining allocations are exactly the `Opt` boxes of finding (d). `backends/go/test_emit_go.py` carries both halves, the idiom rewritten and three aliasing shapes that must keep the copying helper.
    - **(e) DONE, but it does NOT share (a)/(b)'s machinery.** The audit grouped (e) with (a)/(b) as "the same self-rebind analysis". The ownership question is the same shape, but the LOWERING is not: a Go string cannot be mutated, so there is nothing to make destructive, and the accumulation has to move into a `strings.Builder` that spans the loop. `_v3_str_accumulators` decides that per loop: over the WHOLE loop (its condition or iterable included) every assignment to the accumulator must be a `+`/`concat` chain whose leftmost operand is the accumulator itself, the accumulator must appear nowhere else, and the body must contain no `return` (the accumulator is materialized after the loop, which a `return` would skip). A qualifying loop gets `var _revlSB0 strings.Builder` seeded with the current value before it, one `WriteString` per chain piece in place of each rebind, and one `_revlSB0.String()` after it. An accumulator written by a nested loop is caught at the OUTERMOST loop that contains any write to it, so the Builder spans the whole accumulation rather than being rebuilt per outer iteration. `BenchmarkBuildEmitted100` 100 / 37,009 to **8 / 1,912** and `Build1000` 1001 / 3,717,385 to **15 / 34,302**, against the hand `strings.Builder`'s 1 / 704 and 1 / 8,192: a 10x input now costs about 18x the bytes instead of 100x, which is the quadratic gone. The residual gap is the `Grow` the hand version can do because it knows the total length; the emitter does not compute one, so the Builder grows geometrically. `backends/go/test_emit_go.py` pins both halves, the rewrite and two shapes that must keep the plain concatenation (a read of the partial value inside the loop, and a `return` out of it).
    - **(d) NOT DONE, as the audit ordered.** Unchanged: `BenchmarkMaybeEmitted` 1 / 8, and 200 of `BenchmarkBoxedListEmitted`'s 209 allocations. It changes the `Opt`/`Result` encoding the whole v3 tier is written against and wants its own slice.
    - **(g) NOT DONE.** Unchanged: `BenchmarkIndexOfEmitted` 1 / 320, `BenchmarkTakeEmitted` 2 / 328. It is not in the audit's suggested order and was left where the audit put it. One thing found while adding fixtures: `revlStrSlice`'s `[]rune` materialisation substitutes U+FFFD for an invalid byte where the harness's byte-walking `hand.Take` does not, so the two answer differently on invalid UTF-8. That gap belongs to (g), and `invalidText` is deliberately kept out of the shared slice/indexOf fixture list until (g) settles which side is right.
    - **SELF-HOST (item 429's standing rule), verified in the source rather than assumed.** The audit's claim held: of what landed, only (f) needed a port. Checked directly. `selfhost/emit_go.rvl` emits only the `revlDiv`/overflow/overflow32 preambles and never the stdlib or Map preamble, so (h) and (c), both pure helper text, have no self-host site; and it has no `assign`-step self-rebind or accumulator lowering to port for (a)/(b)/(e), since its `emit_stmts` renders a plain `name = value`. Those three carry a DEBT rather than a port: `tests/fixtures/emit_go_corpus/` contains no `List.push` loop, no `Map.set` loop and no `Str` accumulator loop, so the byte-agreement oracle does not reach the new lowerings and passes unchanged. The moment a corpus file uses one of those idioms the self-host must be ported first, or the oracle goes red. (f) was ported: `render_interp` now builds the same `+` chain, and because the `fmt`-versus-`strconv` choice is made from the operand types DURING rendering, `emit_src` renders the function bodies before assembling the import block and reads the two flags off the rendered lines, which is the same "render bodies first so the flags settle" order the reference uses. The now-dead `fmt` field was dropped from `Flags`. `tests/test_selfhost_emit_go.py` (byte agreement over `tests/fixtures/emit_go_corpus/`, `strings.rvl` included) is green, so the reference and the self-host moved together and no new IR key was needed. **On the audit's second self-host observation:** `selfhost/emit_go.rvl` does scan its own input a code point at a time in `while` loops (`trim_str` at :369 and :371 with `charCodeAt`, `split_top` at :381 and :386 and `double_pct` at :769 with `charAt`), and (c) stage one does help it: each read is now allocation-free instead of copying the whole string. But it helps only in bytes. Each read is still O(i), so the self-hosted emitter's own scans stay quadratic in time until (c) stage two lands, which is the strongest single argument for doing stage two.
    - **UNTOUCHED BY DESIGN.** The match IIFE, per the audit's explicit instruction: it measures 0 allocs/op on both sides and inlines. `BenchmarkDescribe*`, `BenchmarkBucket*`, `BenchmarkSumIds*` and `BenchmarkFind*` are all still 0 / 0 on both sides.
    **ONE NON-PERFORMANCE OBSERVATION, noted because the harness tripped over it.** A revl `pub fn` lowers to an UNEXPORTED Go func (`pub fn scan` becomes `func scan`), so no other Go package can call an emitted module. `bench/codegen/go/emitted/*/exports.go` exists only to work around this. Whether `pub` should map to a capitalized Go identifier is a separate question, but the current mapping makes an emitted Go module unusable as a library.

    **WHAT LANDED, PART TWO (2026-09-02, `fix/434-go-codegen-perf-remainder`).** The remainder after the first branch: (c) stage two and (g). Same harness, same `-benchtime` regime, same rule about timings — the machine is shared, so a TIME figure is quoted only as a RATIO between two sizes inside a single run, never as an absolute. (d) is untouched and is now the only open finding.
    - **(g) DONE, and it settles the invalid-UTF-8 question the first branch deferred.** `revlStrIndexOf` is `strings.Index` plus one `utf8.RuneCountInString` over the matched prefix; `revlStrSlice` walks bytes and returns a substring, which shares the receiver's bytes; `revlStrSplit`'s empty-separator branch hands out substrings instead of allocating a fresh one-code-point string per element. `BenchmarkIndexOfEmitted` 1 alloc / 320 B to **0 / 0**, matching the hand form; `BenchmarkTakeEmitted` 2 / 328 to **0 / 0**; a new `BenchmarkCharsEmitted` (`s.split("")` over 78 code points) 80 / 1,912 to **1 / 1,280**, exactly the hand `Chars`. `go build -gcflags='-m'` no longer reports an escaping `[]rune` on any taken path: the two that remain (`string([]rune(s)[a:b])` and `string([]rune(s)[i])`) sit on the invalid-UTF-8 and out-of-range fallback branches. **The semantics decision:** the emitter keeps `[]rune`'s answer, one U+FFFD per invalid byte, because that is what `revlStrCharAt`/`revlStrCharCodeAt` already answer after stage one — so `revlStrSlice` falls back to `[]rune` when an invalid byte lands inside the requested range, and `revlStrIndexOf` falls back when either operand is invalid UTF-8. Valid UTF-8, which is every string a revl program can build, never touches those branches: a valid needle's first byte is never a continuation byte, so a byte match is always at a code-point boundary and `strings.Index` answers the same question as the code-point scan. The harness's `hand.Take` and `hand.IndexOf` moved to the same rule, `invalidText` is now IN the shared fixture list, and `TestStrSliceIsRuneIndexed` pins slice, indexOf and split against the pre-(g) `[]rune` bodies over every fixture at every index from -3 to n+2.
    - **(c) STAGE TWO DONE, but NARROWER than the audit's sketch, and the narrowness is the finding.** `_v3_scan_loops` (`backends/go/emit.py`) recognises a `while` loop as a code-point scan and emits `for _, r := range s`, keeping the body verbatim (its own `i = i + 1` included) and answering each `s.charCodeAt(i)` / `charAt(i)` / `codepoint_at(i)` from the rune already in hand. It fires only where the rewrite is unconditionally equivalent: the condition is exactly `i < s.length()` (inline, or through a local bound to it once and never written again), every write to `i` before the loop is at the top level of the enclosing block with the last assigning literal 0, the only write inside is a trailing `i = i + 1` at the top level of the body, the body has no `continue` of its own, and the string is never reassigned. Those five facts make the loop run exactly `utf8.RuneCountInString(s)` times, which is exactly what `range` yields, so no residual condition check is emitted and `i` is still right after a `break` and after the loop. **Measured:** `BenchmarkScanEmitted78` to `ScanEmitted780` was **86x for a 10x input** (9,863 ns to 852,550 ns in one run) and is now **8.0x to 11.0x over three runs** (323/336/641 ns to 3,169/3,703/5,117 ns), against a hand `for _, r := range s` measuring 9.1x/9.8x/3.6x in the same runs. The quadratic is gone; allocations were already 0 / 0 on both sides after stage one and stay there. `bench/codegen/go/probe.rvl` gained `first_at` (a `return` out of the loop), `run_len` (a `break` with the index read AFTER the loop, which is what pins the bookkeeping) and `step2` (an index advancing by 2, the negative control), all compared against hand equivalents and against `[]rune` over every fixture including invalid UTF-8.
    - **THE NEGATIVE RESULT ON (c) STAGE TWO, which is the part worth reading.** The audit called stage two "the strongest single argument" because `selfhost/emit_go.rvl` scans its own input in `while` loops. **It does not reach them.** `trim_str` (`selfhost/emit_go.rvl:369`, `:371`) is bounded by `a < b` where `b` is a mutable cursor the second loop decrements, and `top_arrow` (`:379`) is bounded by `i < n - 1`; neither is the `i < s.length()` shape. Widening to those needs a condition that merely IMPLIES `i < length`, which in turn needs the residual `if !(cond) { break }` this lowering was able to drop, plus a liveness argument about the mutable bound. So the self-hosted Go emitter's own scans are still O(i) per read. What the rewrite DOES reach, verified by emitting it: `stdlib/str.rvl`'s `str_utf8_bytes` lowers to `for _, _revlR0 := range s`. Nothing in `backends/go/scenarios/`, `backends/go/v3/` or `tests/fixtures/emit_go_corpus/` carries the shape, so the only checked-in golden this branch moves is `backends/go/v3/stdlib/gen.go`, and that moves for (g)'s helper text.
    - **SELF-HOST (item 429's standing rule), checked in the source.** Neither (g) nor (c) stage two needs a port. (g) is pure helper text and `selfhost/emit_go.rvl` never emits the stdlib preamble. (c) stage two is a statement-lowering rewrite and `emit_go.rvl`'s `emit_stmts` renders a plain `while`, so it carries the same DEBT that (a)/(b)/(e) do: `tests/fixtures/emit_go_corpus/` contains no code-point scan loop, so the byte-agreement oracle `tests/test_selfhost_emit_go.py` does not reach the new lowering and passes unchanged. The moment a corpus file uses the idiom the self-host must be ported first or the oracle goes red.

It changes the `Opt`/`Result` encoding the whole v3 tier is written against and still wants its own slice.

435. **TYPESCRIPT CODEGEN PERFORMANCE AUDIT: THE ASYNC COLOUR IS APPLIED PER-FUNCTION, NOT PER-EXPRESSION, SO EVERY `match` IN AN ASYNC BODY BUYS MICROTASK TURNS IT NEVER USES; AND TWO STDLIB LOWERINGS ARE QUADRATIC (2026-09-02).** Audit of the code the TypeScript backend GENERATES, against what a competent TS developer writes by hand for the same revl program. Harness committed at `bench/codegen/typescript/` (`run.mjs`, `cpuprof.mjs`, `emit.py`, `src/*.rvl`, `emitted/*.ts`, `cases/*.ts`, `results/`) and re-runnable standalone. **No timings were taken and none should be quoted from this item**: the audit machine was carrying about a dozen concurrent agents plus six other perf audits, so every number below is load-independent by construction: microtask turns, Promise allocations, code points materialised, array elements copied, and CPU-profile sample shares. Executed on node 26.7.0 against real cordis; every case IMPORTS the emitted function and runs it (nothing is transcribed), declares the emitted fragments it was written against, and `run.mjs` reports `STALE` rather than a number if the emitter has since changed shape. No emitter was edited.

    **❌ STILL OPEN, RE-VERIFIED IN SOURCE ON `bd0f4d19`.** **(a) THE HEADLINE, AND IT IS AN ASYNC-COLOUR BUG. `_v3_match_expr` colours the match by the ENCLOSING FUNCTION, not by whether any arm suspends.** `backends/typescript/emit.py:2453`, `a = "async " if ctx.in_async else ""`, plus the two `(await ({a}({bind}) => ({body}))({tmp}.value))` branches at :2475 and :2498. `ctx.in_async` is true for the whole body of an async-coloured `fn`, so a match whose every arm is a bound variable or a literal still renders as an awaited `async` IIFE wrapping one awaited `async` arrow per bound arm. The arm arrow for `Final(a) => a` is emitted literally as `return (await (async (a) => (a))($revl_match_1.value))`: a Promise allocated around an already-computed string, then awaited. The comment at :2450 calls the extra wrapper "harmless (tsc does not require an `await`)", which is true of type-checking and false of execution. **Measured, per match evaluation: 2 excess microtask turns and 4 excess Promise allocations** (`bench/codegen/typescript/cases/match_sync_arms.ts`; emitted 5 turns / 9 promises, hand-written 3 / 5). The recursive-agent case (`cases/match_async.ts`, 12 matches per call) shows the same 2 turns / 4 promises per match, 24 turns and 48 Promise allocations over one call. CPU profile at equal iteration counts: emitted 730 samples with 16.2% self-time in `EMITTED (anonymous)` frames that the hand-written version does not have at all, and 20.7% in GC against 14.2%; hand-written 367 samples for the identical workload. **PROPOSED FIX, and the cheap one captures all of it.** Emit `async` on the IIFE and on an arm arrow only when the RENDERED body contains `await`, since the emitter already knows this, since `_expr` decides where to insert every `await` and suppresses the await-seed inside arrows (`ctx.in_async and not ctx.in_arrow`, :635), and drop the matching `await` at the call site when it does not. A de-coloured variant that keeps the IIFE and the arm arrows exactly as they are today and changes nothing but the keyword **measures identical to the full hand-written rewrite (3 turns / 5 promises)**, so the whole win is available without touching the lowering's structure. The larger rewrite (lower a match in return position to a plain `switch` with the scrutinee in a local) additionally removes 3 closure allocations per evaluation but buys no further turns. **Cross-tier precedent: the python tier already solved this**, `backends/python/emit.py:2196` `_match_expr(..., awaited=True)` switches from a one-shot lambda to a walrus bind precisely so the arm body's `await` lands in the enclosing frame instead of a wrapper (item 263). The TS tier is the outlier. **Blast radius:** `backends/typescript/golden/async_agent_loop.ts` regenerates; `selfhost/emit_ts.rvl` mirrors this shape byte-exactly (its own header names "the async `match` shape (Opt IIFE + tagged switch, arm-arrows + inner calls awaited)"), so the port is mandatory or `tests/test_selfhost_emit_ts.py` goes red. **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** `_v3_match_expr` is at `backends/typescript/emit.py:2465` and still opens `a = "async " if ctx.in_async else ""` at `:2481` (cites `:2453`); the comment above it still argues the wrapper is harmless.

    **❌ STILL OPEN, RE-VERIFIED IN SOURCE ON `bd0f4d19`.** **(b) SAME ROOT CAUSE, SECOND SITE: a function value whose body only forwards an already-async call is still emitted `async`.** `emit.py:899/921`, `is_async = bool(node.get("async"))` / `prefix = "async " if is_async else ""`. `fn run(prompt) = agent_loop(prompt, (msgs) => model.complete(msgs))` emits `(async (msgs: any) => (ctx.model.complete(msgs)))`. The rendered body contains no `await`, so the `async` adds a resolution hop over the promise the body already returns, and the closure is rebuilt on every call although it captures only `ctx`, which is fixed for the whole activation. **Measured, per operation call: 2 excess microtask turns and 2 excess Promise allocations** (`cases/async_arrow.ts`; emitted 6 / 9, hand-written 4 / 7). Again a de-coloured variant that still allocates the arrow per call measures identical to the hand-written version, so the ticks are the colour and the closure is only allocation. Same fix as (a): the `async` keyword follows the rendered body, not the declared type. Hoisting the arrow to the activation is a separate, smaller, second change. **Blast radius:** `golden/async_fn_values.ts`; `selfhost/emit_ts.rvl` (its header lists "the async ARROW (`async (…) => …`)" and notes "an async arrow flattens its own Promise"). **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** `backends/typescript/emit.py:900` `is_async = bool(node.get("async"))` and `:922` `prefix = "async " if is_async else ""` are unchanged (cites `:899/921`).

    **❌ STILL OPEN, RE-VERIFIED IN SOURCE ON `bd0f4d19`.** **(c) `revlLen` / `revlCharAt` / `revlCharCodeAt` / `revlSlice` rebuild the whole code-point array on EVERY call, so an index scan is quadratic.** `emit.py:2964-2990`, `_REVL_STR_HELPER`: `revlLen` is `Array.from(x).length`, `revlCharAt` is `Array.from(s)[Number(i)]`. Code-point rather than code-unit indexing is correct (docs/strings.md) and is not the problem; materialising the array per call is. Compounding it, the `while` lowering (`_v3_stmt`) re-evaluates the loop condition each iteration, so the idiomatic `while (i < s.length())` calls `revlLen` n times. **Measured, exactly, by intercepting `Array.from` and totalling the code points it produces** for `count_digits` over an n-code-point ASCII string: n=200 -> 80,200; n=400 -> 320,400; n=800 -> 1,280,800; n=1600 -> 5,121,600. Growth is 2n^2 + n against a hand-written n. CPU profile of the emitted scan: **94.8% of self-samples in `revlLen` (47.3%) and `revlCharAt` (45.6%), and 0.5% in `count_digits` itself**. Essentially all of the program's instructions are in the helper, not in the user's logic. **PROPOSED FIX, two tiers.** Cheap and helper-local: memoise the last decoded code-point array (one string, one array) inside the helper block, which collapses all four counts to exactly n with no change to any lowering; measured in `cases/string_scan.ts` as the `memo` column. Caveat worth stating: the memo keys on string identity, so a caller alternating between two equal-but-distinct strings thrashes it, and the guard should be written to fail cheap. Proper: lower an index scan over a `Str` to a single decode, and hoist a loop-invariant `length()` call on a binding the loop body never assigns (a one-line LICM that is trivially sound here because the receiver is a parameter). **Blast radius:** the helper text is emitted into every module that uses a `Str` method, so every golden containing `_REVL_STR_HELPER` regenerates; `selfhost/emit_ts.rvl` carries the helper text and must be ported. **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** `_REVL_STR_HELPER` is at `backends/typescript/emit.py:2992` now (cites `:2964-2990`) and `revlLen` is still `Array.from(x).length`.

    **❌ STILL OPEN, RE-VERIFIED IN SOURCE ON `bd0f4d19`.** **(d) `xs = xs.push(e)` lowers to a whole-array spread, so building an n-element list copies n(n-1)/2 elements.** `emit.py:2277`, `if method == "push": return f"[...{target}, {args[0]}]"`. Value semantics make a copy the honest default, but in the overwhelmingly common `xs = xs.push(e)` the source binding is dead the instant the assignment lands, so the copy is never observed. **Measured, exactly, by intercepting the array iterator** (which forces spread onto its slow path and makes each copied element observable): n=50 -> 1,225 elements copied; n=100 -> 4,950; n=200 -> 19,900; n=400 -> 79,800. Hand-written `xs.push(e)` copies zero. **PROPOSED FIX:** rewrite `x = x.push(e)` to a destructive `x.push(e)` when `x` is a local binding that has not escaped since its last assignment. The safe conservative form is "inside a pure `fn` (G6 already forbids the interesting aliasing), `x` is a `var` local, and `x` is not passed as an argument, returned, or captured anywhere in the loop body". Do NOT apply it to a binding whose old value is still live. **Blast radius:** any golden building a list in a loop; `selfhost/emit_ts.rvl` builds lists this way itself, so the self-host source is one of the beneficiaries. **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** `backends/typescript/emit.py:2305-2306` still returns `[...{target}, {args[0]}]` for `push` (cites `:2277`).

    **(a) AND (b) DONE (2026-09-02), and the audit's cheap fix is the whole win it predicted.** The colour is now decided PER EXPRESSION, from the RENDERED text, in `backends/typescript/emit.py`. `_renders_await(text)` is the entire predicate (the literal `"await "`: every `await` the emitter writes is followed by a space, and `selfhost/emit_ts.rvl` has to mirror it with no regex engine); it errs only towards KEEPING `async`, which is the pre-435 shape, so a false positive costs a microtask turn and never correctness. **(a)** `_v3_match_expr` colours each binding arm-arrow by that arm's own rendered body and the IIFE by the assembled body, dropping the matching `await` at each call site; the IIFE and the arm arrows are structurally UNCHANGED, exactly the variant the audit measured. `match-sync-arms-in-async-fn` goes 5.0 turns / 9.0 promises to **3.0 / 5.0**, equal to hand-written and to the de-coloured variant: **excess 2 turns / 4 promises to 0 / 0**. `match-in-async-fn` is unchanged at 4.2 / 8.3 because every one of its 12 matches takes the arm that genuinely awaits; its residual 2 / 4 per match is the IIFE-plus-arm-arrow structure itself, which only the deliberately-not-taken `switch` rewrite removes. One guard the audit did not name: inside an ARROW the colour stays unconditional, because the await-seed is suppressed there (`in_async and not in_arrow`) so an arm body can be an un-awaited Promise with no `await` in its text, and the arm arrow's `async`/`await` pair is what resolves it. **(b)** the arrow branch drops `async` when the body renders no `await` AND the body IS that un-awaited emission Promise (`_v3_emission_call_node`), narrower than "no await in body", because an `async` arrow over a PLAIN value returns `T` where the slot's type says `Promise<T>`, while `async (p) => e` and `(p) => e` over an emission call are both `(p) => Promise<T>` and stay assignable. `async-arrow-value` goes 6.0 / 9.0 to **4.0 / 7.0**, equal to hand-written: **excess 2 turns / 2 promises to 0 / 0**. Per-call closure allocation is untouched, as the audit ranked it. **Goldens: two lines.** In `golden/async_agent_loop.ts` the sync `Final` arm becomes `return ((answer) => ({ kind: "Final", value: answer }))($revl_match_1.value)` while the awaiting `NeedTool` arm and the IIFE keep their colour; in `golden/async_fn_values.ts` `(async (msgs: any) => (ctx.model.complete(msgs)))` becomes `((msgs: any) => (ctx.model.complete(msgs)))`. `npm run typecheck` (tsc over `golden/**`) is green, which is the type argument executed rather than asserted. **Self-host ported** (`renders_await`, `emission_call_node`, `arm_is_async`, `wrap_match` in `selfhost/emit_ts.rvl`) and checked against the SOURCE, not just the oracle: `emit_ts_corpus/async_module_switch.rvl` already carried a sync `Err(e) => e` arm beside an awaiting `Ok` arm, so (a) is covered, but NO corpus fixture put an emission call in an arrow body, so `async_arrow_emission.rvl` was added for (b): item 429's trap, where a green oracle only means neither side was asked. **Exit conditions (1), (2), (4) and (5) are met**; (3), the quadratic string helpers, is NOT done and neither is (d), the `push` spread.

    **(c) DONE (2026-09-02), and it is the helper-local tier the audit priced, with the whole win it predicted.** `revlLen` / `revlSlice` / `revlCharAt` / `revlCharCodeAt` now share ONE code-point decode, `revlCps`, memoised in `backends/typescript/emit.py`'s `_REVL_STR_HELPER`. **No lowering moved**: the `while` condition still calls `revlLen(s)` on every iteration, exactly as the audit found it, and that call is now O(1), which is what makes the cheap tier sufficient and the LICM/single-decode rewrite unnecessary for this defect. Code points materialised by `Array.from` for `count_digits`, the audit's own measure: n=200 **80,200 -> 200**; n=400 320,400 -> 400; n=800 1,280,800 -> 800; n=1600 **5,121,600 -> 1,600**. Quadratic (x4.0 per doubling) to LINEAR (x2.0), and equal to hand-written and to the `memo` column at every size. The CPU profile inverts with it: the emitted scan goes from 730 samples with 94.8% of self-time in `revlLen` + `revlCharAt` to **6 samples**, against 1205 for the hand-written arm, which now decodes more than the emitted one does because it re-decodes per call. Microtask turns and Promise allocations are unchanged at zero excess, as they were before the fix: (c) was never a tick finding. **TWO slots, not the audit's one.** The audit named the thrash caveat and said the guard should fail cheap; a single slot thrashes on a PAIRWISE scan (compare / merge / diff two strings), which is common enough to matter, and a thrashing cache is exactly the pre-435(c) cost. Two slots make that shape linear too, and since the miss path IS the old code the cache can never cost more than the compare that missed. Note the audit's caveat is stated for reference equality; JS `===` on strings is VALUE equality with a pointer check first, so equal-but-distinct strings hit. The headline is `calls`, Python frames entered: **58284 across the 17 cases, down to 16485**, against 13614 for the hand-written comparators. Twelve of the seventeen cases now enter EXACTLY as many frames as the hand-written arm.

One temp name serves any nesting depth, because the walrus sits in a conditional expression's CONDITION, which python evaluates before either branch: an inner operation has finished reading `_bi` before an outer one rebinds it, and the outer branch reads what the outer bind just wrote. `arith.sum_squares` **8002 frames to 2** (hand-written 2), `list_build.build` 402 to 2, `maps.fill` 402 to 2, `maps.probe` 402 to 2, `transforms.list_sort` 30090 to 9685 (hand-written 9685, so 3.11x to 1.00x). **It costs about two executed opcodes per bounded operation**, which is why `arith` moves 1.22x to 1.29x in `ops` and `maps.fill` 3.41x to 3.56x: the inline form loads two module constants where the call loaded one global. That is the trade the finding predicted (`ops` under-prices a frame), and it is recorded here rather than buried, because a reader comparing the two `ops` columns will otherwise think something broke.

The lambda is what makes the shadow work. Deciding it needs the set of names bound in the ENCLOSING FUNCTION, which neither `_match_expr` nor its self-host mirror is given, so it is a threading change and not a spelling one. **Note while there: the `awaited` payload binder, which has spelled itself with a walrus since item 263, carries that shadowing bug today.** It is not exercised by any fixture and was not fixed here; it belongs with whatever closes the sync half.
