437. **RUST CODEGEN PERFORMANCE AUDIT: 57% OF EVERY `String::from` THE EMITTER WRITES IS A HEAP ALLOCATION FOR A LITERAL THAT IS NEVER STORED, AND ITEM 284's IN-PLACE SELF-APPEND MISSES THE SHAPE THE SELF-HOST COMPILER ACTUALLY USES (2026-09-02).** Audit of the rust `backends/rust/emit.py` EMITS, against the rust a competent developer would write by hand for the same semantics. Harness landed at `bench/codegen/rust/` (12 benchmark programs in revl, 12 hand-written comparators, a runner that builds both into ONE crate under a counting global allocator and asserts they agree before reporting, plus `census.py`, which counts each wasteful shape in the rust emitted for the four self-host stages that build). **NO WALL-CLOCK NUMBER WAS TAKEN and none is quoted here.** The machine was running about a dozen concurrent agents; a duration measured under unknown load is not evidence and neither is a ratio of two durations sampled at different moments, so `run.py` takes no timing unless `--timing` is passed and the evidence below is entirely allocation counts, heap bytes, generated-code census and complexity class, all of which are properties of the generated code and identical on an idle host. No instruction-count tool was available either (no valgrind, cachegrind or perf on this macOS arm64 host). A timing pass is a one-flag re-run on a quiet machine. Item 277 is the reason for that discipline: it records a plausible rust perf change here that REGRESSED the self-host lexer by 28%, which is exactly what an allocation count would have caught and an intuition did not.

    **The census, over 13,891 lines of rust emitted for `selfhost/{lexer,parser,checker,lower}.rvl`:** 4,895 `.clone()`, 3,920 `String::from(`, of which 1,235 are `&String::from(` (a literal allocated onto the heap to be handed to a helper whose parameter is `&str`) and 988 are `== String::from(` / `!= String::from(` (a literal allocated to be compared and dropped). Those 2,223 sites are 57% of every `String::from` in the emitted self-host compiler, and every one of them is a heap allocation whose value is never stored anywhere. Also 332 index reads cloned, 65 self-appends through `concat`, 3 for-loop iterable clones.

    (a) **❌ STILL OPEN, RE-VERIFIED IN SOURCE ON `bd0f4d19`.** **Self-append through `concat` is not covered by item 284, and it is the shape the self-host emitters use.** Measured on `bench/codegen/rust/programs/concat_append.rvl`: 729,599 heap allocations and 97.2 MB against 2,425 and 212 KB hand-written, so 301x the allocations and 458x the bytes, and O(n^2) copies against O(n) amortised. `_v3_self_append_inplace` (`backends/rust/emit.py:5049`) rewrites `out = out.push(x)` in place but dispatches through `_v3_inplace_persistent` (`:5039`), which lists only `push`/`set`/`remove`; item 284's own comment excludes `concat` because "its receiver type is not known at this node". For the SELF-ASSIGN shape that is no longer true: the receiver is a bare local, so `ctx.var_types[target_name]` resolves it, and item 284's liveness argument (the assign rebinds the receiver over its own value, so the pre-image is unreachable) carries over verbatim. `selfhost/emit_go.rvl`, `emit_java.rvl`, `emit_ts.rvl` and `checker.rvl` accumulate their output through exactly `out = out.concat(...)`; the census counts 65 such sites in the four stages that emit. The Str spelling `s = s + p` never reaches that function at all, because it is a `bin` node handled at `:4321` and turned into `format!("{}{}", s, p)`, a fresh String per iteration: measured separately at 5,999 allocations and 84.3 MB against 13 and 32 KB. **Fix:** add a `concat` arm to `_v3_inplace_persistent` split by receiver type (`v.extend(arg.iter().cloned())` for List, `s.push_str(&arg)` for Str) and a `+` arm to `_v3_self_append_inplace`. **Blast radius:** neither `backends/rust/golden/*.rs` contains the shape, so goldens are byte-unchanged. `tests/fixtures/emit_rust_corpus/{strings,control}.rvl` do not contain it either, which means the self-host byte-agreement oracle stays GREEN WITHOUT A PORT. That is the item-429 trap, not a free pass: port to `selfhost/emit_rust.rvl` AND add a corpus fixture, or the divergence is invisible by construction. **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** `_v3_self_append_inplace` is at `backends/rust/emit.py:5066` now (cites `:5049`).

    (b) **❌ STILL OPEN, RE-VERIFIED IN SOURCE ON `bd0f4d19`.** **String literals are allocated for slots that borrow.** `_rust_v3_lit` (`:823`) renders every Str literal as `String::from(..)` unconditionally. `_v3_builtin` (`:4735` onward) then writes `&{arg}` for `concat`/`indexOf`/`split`/`join`/`startsWith`/`endsWith`, whose helper-trait parameters are all `&str`, so the emitted code allocates a String purely to take a reference to it; and the `==`/`!=` fall-through at `:4343` compares against a freshly allocated `String` where `String: PartialEq<&str>` would compare in place. Measured: `literal_arg` 400,000 allocations and 5.50 MB against 40,000 and 0.67 MB (10x); `str_eq_literal` 240,000 allocations and 1.12 MB against ZERO and zero. Census: 1,235 + 988 = 2,223 sites. **Fix:** render a Str literal as the bare `&'static str` when the slot is one of `_BORROW_ARG_BUILTINS` or an `==`/`!=` operand whose other side is `Str`. **Blast radius:** no golden contains `&String::from(`; `backends/rust/test_emit_rust.py:1018` pins `m.remove(&String::from("a"))` and would need updating; no corpus fixture exercises it, so again port `selfhost/emit_rust.rvl:531` and add a fixture rather than trusting a green oracle. **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** `_rust_v3_lit` is at `backends/rust/emit.py:830` (cites `:823`) and its docstring still reads "strings are owned `String`".

    (c) **❌ STILL OPEN, RE-VERIFIED IN SOURCE ON `bd0f4d19`.** **`Str.indexOf` materialises BOTH operands as `Vec<char>` on every call.** The emitted prelude (`:4877`) opens with `let hay: Vec<char> = self.chars().collect(); let nee: Vec<char> = needle.chars().collect();` and then scans naively. Measured: 1,500 allocations and 12.97 MB for 300 calls over a 10.8 KB haystack, against ZERO and zero hand-written. **Fix:** `self.find(needle).map(|b| self[..b].chars().count() as i64).unwrap_or(-1)`, which preserves the codepoint-index contract on every input (empty needle gives 0, absent gives -1, non-ASCII gives the codepoint index) and gets `str::find`'s two-way search instead of the O(n*m) walk. **This is the cheapest fix in the item and has the SMALLEST blast radius of any of them:** one function in the prelude, no golden contains the prelude (both checked-in goldens are stdlib-free per item 282), and `selfhost/emit_rust.rvl` does not carry the prelude text at all, so no self-host port is needed. Take this one first. **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** the prelude's `let hay: Vec<char>` is at `backends/rust/emit.py:4896` (cites `:4877`).

    (d) **❌ STILL OPEN, RE-VERIFIED IN SOURCE ON `bd0f4d19`.** **Every `List` index read clones the element.** `:4502` emits `({target})[({index}) as usize].clone()` unconditionally, so `xs[i] == probe` allocates a String, compares it and drops it. Measured on `list_index.rvl`: 150,000 allocations and 572 KB against ZERO and zero. Census: 332 sites. **Fix:** reuse item 282's read-only-position classification (a `==` operand, a `&str` builtin receiver or argument, an interpolation operand) and borrow there. Larger analysis than (a) to (c), and it does touch goldens and needs the `emit_rust.rvl` port. **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** `backends/rust/emit.py:4519` still emits `({target})[({index}) as usize].clone()` (cites `:4502`).

    (e) **❌ STILL OPEN, RE-VERIFIED IN SOURCE ON `bd0f4d19`.** **A param-less fn whose body is a constant list of literals is rebuilt on every call.** `selfhost/lexer.rvl`'s `fn keywords() -> List[Str]` is consulted per identifier token and emits 35 `String::from` plus a `Vec` every time. Measured on `const_list.rvl`: 720,000 allocations and 20.36 MB for 20,000 lookups against a 35-entry table, versus ZERO and zero for the `static KEYWORDS: &[&str]` a rust developer writes. revl `List` is persistent with no in-place mutation, so a shared immutable table is observationally identical. Ranked below (a) to (d) on EFFORT, not on win: hoisting it properly is a return-type change (`&'static [&'static str]` plus a read-only surface for it), which is the same class of calling-convention change item 282 took for `&str` params and item 277 showed can go the wrong way if done naively. **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** unchanged.

    (f) **❌ STILL OPEN, RE-VERIFIED IN SOURCE ON `bd0f4d19`.** **`for x of v` clones the iterable whenever `v` is referenced more than once ANYWHERE in the body.** `:5181` sends the iterable through `_by_value_tail`, which consults `ctx.multi_use`, built at `:5359` as a whole-body reference COUNT with no liveness. So building an accumulator and then walking it once clones the whole thing, including every String field, because the item-284 in-place `push` receiver still counts as a by-value use. Measured on `for_over_local.rvl`: 120,016 allocations and 4.38 MB against 60,015 and 2.28 MB, exactly 2.00x. Census finds only 3 sites in the self-host stages, so the real-world win is small and it is ranked last among the fixes. **Narrow provable fix:** move rather than clone when every other reference to the name is in a statement strictly BEFORE the loop and the loop is not itself nested inside another loop (a move inside an outer loop would fail on the second iteration). **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** `_by_value_tail` is reached from `backends/rust/emit.py:5080` and `:5153` (cites `:5181`) and `ctx.multi_use` is still a whole-body reference count with no liveness.

    (g) **❌ STILL OPEN, RE-VERIFIED IN SOURCE ON `bd0f4d19`.** **`Str.length()` in a `while` condition is recomputed per iteration. ANALYTIC ONLY, NOT MEASURED.** `revl_length` on a `str` is `chars().count()`, so an O(n) walk runs n times and the loop is O(n^2). There is NO allocation evidence for this (0 versus 0 on both sides) and no timing was taken, so it is a complexity argument, not a measurement, and it is labelled as such. It is also SMALL in practice: the census finds 746 `while (i < x.revl_length())` sites but only 3 with a `Str` receiver, the other 743 being `Vec`, where `revl_length` is `self.len() as i64` and O(1). Recorded so the shape is on file, ranked last of all. **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** `chars().count()` is at `backends/rust/emit.py:4891`.

    **NEGATIVE RESULTS, measured and fine.** (1) `out = out.push(x)`, item 284's own shape, is EXACTLY what a rust developer writes: 17 allocations and 2,097,152 bytes on BOTH sides, identical to the byte. Item 284 holds and this benchmark is now its regression guard. (2) Pure `Int` arithmetic costs the emitter nothing extra: 0 allocations both sides, and the emitted `checked_add(..).expect(..)` is character-for-character what the comparator has to write, because trapping `Int` is revl SEMANTICS and not emitter waste. There is nothing to win on arithmetic. (3) The `Arc<Box<dyn Svc>>` double indirection on every `requires` is NOT emitter waste: `cordis::Context::require<T>` is bounded `T: Send + Sync + 'static` with no `?Sized`, so `require::<dyn Model>` does not compile against the pinned cordis-rs 0.3.0 and `Box<dyn Model>` is the only expressible form. Removing the extra pointer chase means adding `?Sized` upstream in cordis-rs, per the fork-and-PR rule for the rs runtime, not changing the emitter. (Noted in passing: `backends/rust/emit.py`'s own module docstring claims it emits `ctx.provide_arc("key", Arc::new(impl) as Arc<dyn Svc>)`, which is not what it emits; the docstring is stale.) (4) The item-277/282 `slice(i, i+1)` front-walk residual is real and re-measured at 8,000 allocations against 3, but it is already on file and item 277 records that the obvious fix regressed the self-host lexer, so it is re-measured here and deliberately NOT re-proposed.

    **Suggested order, cheapest first: (c), then (b), then (a).** (c) touches one prelude function with no golden and no self-host exposure. (b) is the largest measured allocation count in the census. (a) is the largest per-site win and the one that needs the item-429 discipline of a new corpus fixture alongside the `selfhost/emit_rust.rvl` port. `backends/rust/emit.py` for all of them, plus `selfhost/emit_rust.rvl` and `tests/fixtures/emit_rust_corpus/` for (a), (b) and (d).

    **LANDED (c), (b) and (a), in that order, on `fix/437-rust-codegen-perf` (2026-09-02).** Every figure below is a re-run of `bench/codegen/rust/run.py` and `census.py` after the change; NO WALL CLOCK WAS TAKEN, on the same reasoning the audit gives above, and the machine was again running about a dozen concurrent agents.
    * **(c) DONE.** `revl_index_of` is now `self.find(needle)` with the byte offset converted to a codepoint index by counting the prefix. **1,500 allocations and 12.97 MB -> 0 and 0**, which is the hand-written comparator exactly. Verified as predicted: no golden carries the prelude and `selfhost/emit_rust.rvl` carries no prelude text at all, so there was no port. The stale `provide_arc` module docstring the audit noted in passing is corrected in the same commit.
    * **(b) DONE, and wider than the audit scoped it.** A `Str` literal now renders as the bare `&'static str` in three read-only slots: the `RevlStrOps`/`RevlStrListOps` `&str` argument slots, the `==`/`!=` operands, and the item-282 borrowed-param call path, which the audit had not separated out and which turned out to be 588 of the sites. **`literal_arg` 400,000 allocations and 5.50 MB -> 120,000 and 1.38 MB; `str_eq_literal` 240,000 and 1.12 MB -> 0 and 0.** Census: **1,235 literal-into-a-`&str`-slot -> 0, 988 literal-compared-to-a-`Str` -> 0**, all 2,223 sites gone, total `String::from(` **3,920 -> 1,697**. Two receiver-overloaded methods needed care: `indexOf` on a `List[Str]` takes `&String`, so it requires a certainly-`Str` receiver, while `concat` on a `List` takes `&Vec<T>`, which a `Str` literal can never be, so a literal there already proves the `Str` overload. The `==` rule borrows unless the emitter POSITIVELY knows the other operand is a non-`Str` type, because a site that compiles today has that operand rendering as `String` or `&str` and both carry `PartialEq<&str>`; requiring a certainly-`Str` other side would have left every `for`-binding and extern-result operand untouched, which is most of them. `literal_arg`'s residual 3x is the one `indexOf` whose receiver is a `for` binding the emitter cannot type.
    * **(a) DONE, both spellings.** `_v3_inplace_persistent` gained a `concat` arm split by receiver type (`s.push_str(..)` / `v.extend(x.iter().cloned())`) and `_v3_self_append_inplace` gained a `+` arm, `_v3_self_append_plus`. **`concat_append` 729,599 allocations and 97.2 MB -> 4,825 and 236 KB** against 2,425 and 212 KB hand-written, so the O(n^2) is now O(n) and the residual 2x is the per-element clone revl's persistent `List` semantics require (the comparator may move, the emitter may not). **`str_append` 5,999 and 84.3 MB -> 13 and 32,768 B, identical to the comparator.** Census: **65 self-appends via `concat` -> 0**. The audit's receiver-type argument held, and one extra rule closes the last ten sites: a receiver `var_types` cannot name, appending something certainly `Str`, is a `Str` receiver, because `List[T].concat` takes a `List[T]`. `list_append`, item 284's own control, is unchanged at 17 and 2,097,152 B on both sides.
    * **RUST DID NOT NEED THE GO TIER'S ANALYSIS.** Item 434 needed `_v3_self_rebind_locals`, a whole-body proof of unique ownership, because a Go slice header aliases silently and nothing in the language catches a second live owner. Rust needs none of it: a second live owner can only arise from a move, rustc refuses a move-then-reuse (E0382), and every by-value move this backend emits clones first, so item 284's uniqueness argument is discharged by the borrow checker on exactly the code that already compiles. The rewrite stays local. One guard was added that the ownership argument does NOT cover: an appended operand that reads the receiver (`s = s + s`) would take a shared borrow of a value already borrowed mutably (E0502) where the persistent form compiled, so `_v3_mentions_name` refuses that shape.
    * **THE ITEM-429 TRAP, CHECKED DIRECTLY RATHER THAN TRUSTED TO THE ORACLE.** `selfhost/emit_rust.rvl` was read for each shape instead of relying on a green byte-agreement run. It carries NO stdlib `builtin`/`len` surface and NO item-282 borrow analysis, so (c), the `&str`-slot half of (b), and the `concat` half of (a) have no mirror there and no port. The two halves that DO have a mirror were ported: (b)'s `==`/`!=` borrow into `render_bin`, and (a)'s `+` self-append into the `assign` step, with `borrowed_str_lit`, `eq_operand_borrowable`, `borrow_str_arg`, `mentions_name` and `self_append_plus`. **`tests/fixtures/emit_rust_corpus/perf_shapes.rvl` is the new fixture**, holding the `==` borrow in both operand orders with a typed and an un-inferable operand, a non-`Str` `==` that must not move, the `+` self-append, and a `+` whose target is not the receiver. It is deliberately free of any `builtin`/`len` node, since those are outside the port's covered subset. The `concat` spelling of the self-append therefore still has no fixture, because there is nothing for it to diverge from until the stdlib surface is ported.
    * **VERIFIED:** `bench/codegen/rust/run.py` (all twelve build, agree and report), `census.py`, `backends/rust/test_emit_rust.py` (114 passed, including the `cargo check` over emitted output), the byte-agreement oracle over all 19 corpus fixtures, and `tests/test_selfhost_emit_rust.py` in full at (b) (138 passed, including `test_selfhost_stages_cargo_build_and_run`, which builds and runs the four self-host stages natively over the 2,223 changed sites). **NOT VERIFIED:** `test_selfhost_stages_cargo_build_and_run` was not re-run after (a) landed, and neither full `tests/` suite was run on either interpreter. The host was carrying about forty concurrent test processes across ten agents and reds under that load were not reproducing, so the gate was left to the merge owner rather than reported from noise.
    * **LEFT, as the audit scoped them:** (d) index-read clones, 332 census sites, unchanged; (e) the constant-list rebuild; (f) the for-loop iterable clone, 3 sites; (g) the `Str.length()` complexity note, analytic only. All four negative results are untouched, and the item-277/282 `slice` residual was left alone as the audit instructed.

438. **PETRI-NET REACHABILITY AS A COMPILE-TIME LIVENESS ANALYZER (2026-09-02, ported idea, VERIFIED ABSENT).** Grepped: revl has ZERO Petri results anywhere in the tree, and no liveness analysis of any kind. The static guarantees are all STRUCTURAL: G2 provisions are disjoint per `(key, realm)`, G3 the graph is acyclic, G7 teardown is LIFO-complete. None of them answers a REACHABILITY question, so a composition that is structurally admissible can still reach a dead state at runtime: two consumers each holding a provision the other waits on, or a `subscribe merge(a, b)` fan-in whose sources are consumed elsewhere so the merge never becomes enabled. Item 130's pointwise admission rules 3.1 and 3.6 check each source IN ISOLATION, which is exactly the gap: they cannot see an interleaving.
    **The shape.** A `revl analyze` mode, NOT a runtime: derive a net from the composition IR (provisions and coeffects as places, activation bodies as transitions), then bounded BFS over the marking graph to find dead states, with S-invariants to prove boundedness where the graph is too large. It becomes another fold in the admission gate, so the result is a REFUSAL naming the deadlocked cycle rather than a crash at 3am, which is the same shape items 427 and 428 landed for their checks.
    **Why this is a real port and not a rewrite.** The engine is dependency-free structural mathematics (nets, markings, enablement, bounded reachability, Martinez-Silva signed elimination for S-invariants); none of it needs to know anything about revl. The revl-side work is the DERIVATION from IR to net and the refusal wording, not the algorithm.
    **Open questions before slicing.** (1) What is a place: a provision key, a `(key, realm)` pair, or a coeffect? G2's own unit is `(key, realm)`, which argues for that. (2) Bounded BFS needs a bound, and a refusal that fires only under a bound is a partial guarantee that must SAY so (item 418's lesson: a check must not claim more than it establishes). (3) Does a dead state refuse admission, or warn? A false positive that blocks a legal composition is worse than the deadlock for adoption, so this likely starts as `revl analyze` and only becomes a gate once the false-positive rate is measured. Relates to 130 (streams), 418 (do not overclaim what a check proves), 426 (composition as the analyzed unit).

439. **A2A 1.0.0 TRANSPORT BINDING FOR REMOTE PROVIDERS (2026-09-02, ported idea, VERIFIED ABSENT).** Grepped: revl has NO A2A surface at all. Its interop is strictly revl-to-revl: UDS seams, `RemoteScope` realms, cross-tier placement, and item 151's two-composition topology. So a revl composition can consume another revl composition and nothing else.
    **Why now.** Item 424 gap (c) decided the SEMANTICS this needs and deliberately left the transport abstract: a remote provider is a ROW whose provider is synthesized, remoteness is an admission fact rather than a wiring difference, transport failure is a WITHDRAWAL by default (reusing R2/R3) with `on_failure(result)` as the opt-in, every returned value is `Untrusted[T]`, and a generated client does NOT re-admit the callee (337: the receiver re-compiles from its own source; a client is the sender). An A2A binding makes that concrete without reopening any of it.
    **The shape.** A service declaration whose provider is spelled remote over A2A synthesizes an adapter component that crosses the seam with A2A task semantics (Agent Cards, Task/Message/Part/Artifact, Send/Stream/Cancel over JSON-RPC 2.0, HTTP/REST, SSE, gRPC). Every guarantee still applies AT THE BOUNDARY: G1 declared-only access, the capability cone, tickets, and the F5/F6/F7 redaction that landed today.
    **What must be decided, not assumed.** (1) A2A's Task lifecycle is long-running and streaming; revl's emission model is a single crossing with an inverse. Does an A2A Task map to one emission, to a stream (item 130), or to a session (250)? This is the load-bearing question and it is not obvious. (2) An external agent is not a revl composition, so NOTHING about it is checked: its Agent Card is a CLAIM. That makes every A2A provider item 329's untrusted-author case by construction, and the returned `Untrusted[T]` of 424(c) is necessary but probably not sufficient. (3) Version honesty: the claim must be "A2A 1.0.0", never "A2A", because the protocol moves.
    **Why it is worth doing.** It is the difference between revl components composing only with each other and revl components consuming the wider agent ecosystem as CHECKED provisions. Depends on 424(c) and 426 S1 (the row table). Relates to 337 (polyglot admission mesh), 329 (untrusted-author profile), 151 (two-composition topology).

440. **EXTERN CALL TIERS: THE THIRD TIER AND THE RE-ISSUE SEAM (2026-09-02).** A ported-idea review proposed classifying extern calls into read / idempotent / non-idempotent tiers with a journalled dispatch and a fail-closed ambiguous outcome on restart. **Most of that already exists as item 309 and this item records only the genuine remainder**, because the proposal as stated would have duplicated landed work. What 309 already does, verified in `src/revl/recovery.py`: the WAL journals each effect as it commits; recovery branches on `undo_idempotent`; an UNKEYED inverse whose single at-most-once attempt is spent refuses with `outcome="unknown"` and the operator hint "second attempt cannot be proven safe"; a KEYED one is classified `replay: free` by the `--recovery` audit. That is journal, branch by tier, fail-closed on ambiguity, already shipped.
    **❌ OPEN, RE-VERIFIED IN SOURCE ON `bd0f4d19`.** **(a) THERE IS NO READ TIER.** 309's register is two-valued (keyed or not). A pure READ extern is safely re-dispatchable on recovery with no key and no reconciliation, because it changes nothing, and today it is treated as unkeyed and therefore ambiguous. That is a fail-closed error in the SAFE direction, so it is a usability defect rather than a soundness one, but it makes recovery ask an operator about calls that never needed asking. Note revl already knows which externs are pure, so the tier may be derivable rather than declared. **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** no read tier exists in the shipped source; 309's register is still two-valued.
    **❌ OPEN, RE-VERIFIED IN SOURCE ON `bd0f4d19`.** **(b) THE RE-ISSUE SEAM IS DEFERRED, AND THE CODE SAYS SO.** `recovery.py` carries `TODO(309-slice3)`: an owed deferred emission whose extern is `idempotent(key: p)` MAY be auto-fired on recovery, since the descriptor carries the key and the fire is dedup-safe even if the pre-crash flush landed. It is not done because firing requires re-invoking the emission host body and the minimal fresh-process recover has no runtime for it. So the keyed tier's advantage is currently CLASSIFIED but not ACTED ON: a keyed owed emission is reported as free to replay and then left for a human anyway. **RE-CHECK 2026-09-02:** `src/revl/recovery.py:445` still carries the `TODO(309-slice3)` comment this finding quotes.
    **Exit:** (1) a read tier, derived from the existing purity classification if that is sound, so a read never reaches an operator as ambiguous; (2) the item-309 slice-3 re-issue seam, gated by the item-33 policy knob the TODO names, so a keyed owed emission can actually be auto-fired; (3) a test that a read-tier extern recovers with no operator prompt, and that a non-idempotent one still refuses. Relates to 309 (the register and its partial order), 245 (session commit), A8 (WAL discharge), 418 (the formal layer now models the three teardown entry kinds, which is the adjacent distinction).

441. **TERMINATION IS AGENT-OWNED, AND NOTHING IN THE LANGUAGE DECIDES WHEN A TASK IS DONE (2026-09-02, ported idea, VERIFIED ABSENT).** Grepped: no goal contract, no acceptance criteria, no termination controller anywhere in revl (the only hits are in `forks/stc-go`, unrelated). revl's agent story ends at the admission gate: `revl mcp serve` gives an agent `revl_check` and `revl_admit`, and the gate answers "may this run", but NOTHING answers "is this done". The agent decides for itself when to stop.
    **Why this is the same defect class revl already spends effort closing.** Items 427 F2/F3/F4 were all one shape: the operator is shown one thing and the system acts on another. Agent-owned termination is that shape at the task level. The operator approves a goal, the agent decides unilaterally whether it met it, and there is no artifact the operator can check the claim against. A gate that judges every crossing but never judges completion leaves the largest decision unjudged.
    **The shape.** The agent DRAFTS acceptance criteria; the system FREEZES them into an immutable goal contract at activation; from then on a deterministic state machine, reading observable state rather than the agent's own reply, owns every termination decision, with an auditable trail per turn. In revl's idiom this is not new machinery: criteria are revl functions over observable state, verifiers are declared services, the contract is a composition-declared object frozen at activation, and an attempt to effect past a satisfied or violated contract fires a class-(c) ticket exactly as an unapproved crossing does today.
    **What must be decided, not assumed.** (1) Who may amend a frozen contract, and does amendment invalidate the run's prior approvals? The honest default is that it does, per item 427 F4's grant-invalidation rule. (2) Criteria are drafted BY the agent, so a contract is only as good as the drafting; freezing an inadequate criterion is not safety, it is a durable mistake, and the design must say what the operator reviews and when. (3) The value-of-continuation estimate the source system computes across candidate actions is the part most likely to be wrong here: revl has no reward model and should not acquire one casually. Start with satisfied / violated / undecided and no scoring. Relates to 427 (shown versus enforced), 246 (typed approval), 344 (standing grants), 251 (distillation).

442. **DELEGATION IS NOT A VERB: A COMPONENT CANNOT HAND A SCOPED, REVOCABLE REFERENCE TO ANOTHER (2026-09-02, ported idea).** revl already ATTENUATES authority on spawn (`lower.py:10671`: a capability "attenuates on delegation: the child's ceiling"), so the concept of a narrowed child authority exists. What does not exist is a way for one component to hand a scoped reference to one of its own provisions to a component that is not its child, with the HANDOFF ITSELF checked. Today the options are to widen the consumer's declared requires (permanent, not scoped) or to route every call through the holder (correct but eliminates the point).
    **The shape.** `delegate` as a language-level crossing whose receipt is minted BY THE GATE, not by either party: a hash over the delegated surface, an expiry, and a revocation hook wired to the provider's own withdrawal, bound to the consumer's realm. A forged or replayed delegation refuses at the seam the same way item 337's unjudged addresses now do, and the receipt is the artifact an operator reads.
    **Why it matters more after 439.** A remote provider over A2A is close to useless without delegation: every call would otherwise need its own approval, which is the ergonomic failure that pushes people to over-grant. 439 and 442 are the same feature seen from two ends.
    **Open questions.** (1) Revocation versus G7: a delegated reference revoked mid-activation is a withdrawal under a consumer that did not declare it, which is the interaction G7 governs and 426 R1 already flagged as blocked. (2) Does a delegation transfer or share? Sharing needs no G2 change; transfer does, since G2's unit is `(key, realm)`. (3) Depth: does a delegate re-delegate, and if so does the receipt chain or flatten? An unbounded chain is a capability cone nobody can enumerate, which breaks G8. Relates to 439 (remote providers), 337 (seam judgement), 294 (parameterized capabilities), 421 F1 (token attenuation), 426 (rows and claims).

443. PARTIALLY LANDED 2026-09-02, now ON MAIN (`92d8b7c6`, PR #169; branch `feat/443-estop` deleted after landing, verified ancestor of main): the py tier and the formal layer. The five non-py tiers keep their cooperative teardown and have no E-Stop, deliberately — see **Not done** in PR #169. GitHub issue #122 stays open for those. **E-STOP: THERE IS NO OPERATOR HALT THAT IS NOT A GRACEFUL UNWIND (2026-09-02, ported idea, VERIFIED ABSENT).** Grepped: no `e-stop`, `estop` or `emergency` anywhere in revl. Every stop revl has is COOPERATIVE: teardown replays inverses LIFO, faults route through residue records, withdrawal propagates to dependents. That is exactly right for a composition fault and exactly wrong for an operator emergency. When a human hits the button during a class-(c) storm or a runaway loop with irreversible effects in flight, unwinding 200 brackets first is not a safe answer; it is a long answer.
    **The honest semantics.** Stop dispatching NEW crossings immediately, report what was in flight, and mark the ambiguous ones ambiguous. That is a different verdict from both commit and abort, and item 418's newly-corrected G7 model is where it has to be stated, since G7 now carries the activation's verdict explicitly and `replaysUnder` is read off the teardown contract's table. An E-Stop verdict is a third column in that table, and adding it is a formal-layer change before it is a runtime change.
    **It gives item 440 its counterpart.** 440 records that revl's extern tiers classify a call as ambiguous when its at-most-once attempt may or may not have landed. E-Stop is precisely the event that CREATES that state deliberately: it lands between the journal entry and the completion record, so the ambiguous tier is not an edge case any more, it is the designed outcome of an operator halt. The two features are stronger together than either alone.
    **The shape.** A `revl estop` verb on the CLI and MCP surfaces, held as an operator authority (not something a composition or an agent may invoke on itself, which is the whole point), plus an in-flight inventory in the residue record so the report says what was interrupted rather than what was unwound.
    **Open questions.** (1) Is E-Stop expressible as a verdict in the item-418 teardown model without weakening G7's completeness theorem, or does G7 become conditional on the verdict? (2) What happens to a bracket whose inverse is ITSELF in flight when the stop arrives? (3) Does an E-Stop composition ever resume, or is the instance dead and recovery the only path back? Relates to 418 (the G7 verdict model), 440 (ambiguous tiers), 309 (at-most-once attempts), 397 (residue records).
    **DESIGN AND PY-TIER IMPLEMENTATION, `feat/443-estop` (docs/design/443-estop.md).** The three open questions are answered, formal layer first. (1) **G7 does not weaken and does not become conditional.** Its completeness (`teardown_replays_all`) and soundness (`teardown_only_witnessed`) were already stated relative to `replaysUnder v` after item 418's correction, so they extend to the new `Verdict.halted` UNCHANGED and hold with an empty replay set — no hypothesis added to either. What changed is two COROLLARIES that quantified over every verdict while assuming every verdict settles: `G7.bracket_replays_under_every_verdict` and `Semantics.replays_or_discharges` now carry `v.settles = true`, with the E-Stop counter-instance proved beside each so the hypothesis is exhibited as load-bearing rather than left as an unexplained weakening. The general statement that replaces the dichotomy is `Semantics.disposition_trichotomy`: every (kind, verdict) pair has exactly one of THREE dispositions — replayed, discharged, or **stranded** (registered, not run, and NOT dropped) — and `Semantics.book_lengths_add` proves the three lists partition the stack under every verdict. Stranded is not a synonym for discharged: discharge RELEASES the inverse and the witness, and an E-Stop must keep both, because `revl recover` is what reads them back. (2) **A bracket whose inverse is in flight becomes that activation's single `estop-ambiguous` record.** The halt is a CUT at index `k` into the interrupted verdict's replay order — `haltCompleted` / `haltAmbiguous` / `haltUnattempted` — with `halt_ambiguity_is_at_most_one` and `halt_books_are_total` proving the split is bounded and total. Reconciliation is item 309's existing rule (keyed → re-issuable, unkeyed → refuse with `outcome: unknown`), reached deliberately instead of by accident. (3) **The instance is DEAD; recovery is the only path back.** No resume: the body was cut mid-step and the runtime cannot know whether the in-flight crossing landed. Because the halt strands rather than discharges and writes no `discharge` record, the WAL discharge-descriptors with nothing behind them are exactly what is owed — **an E-Stop is deliberately shaped to look like a CRASH to `revl recover`**, which already has a proven answer for one. **What landed:** `Verdict.halted` + the three-way disposition in `formal/RevL/Semantics.lean`, the E-Stop column and the halt cut in `G7_LifoComplete.lean` (13 new theorems, all registered in the axioms and non-vacuity gates); the third column and two new residue kinds (`estop-stranded`, `estop-ambiguous`) in `docs/design/teardown-contract.md`; a process-global latch plus a cross-process latch FILE in `backends/python/runtime.py`, checked at every seam that dispatches or accepts a crossing (`plug`, acquire, witnessed, compensate, deferred flush, approval crossing), with `Frame._guard` stranding instead of replaying and `drain` committing nothing; `revl estop --latch/--wal/--report/--clear` and `revl run --estop-latch`; `revl_estop` / `revl_estop_report` on MCP, gated on a NEW `estop` operator verb (item 55) whose target set is the whole composition — never folded into `unload` or `commit`, and with no in-language surface at all, which is what makes "a composition may not halt itself" structural. **Stated cost, not hidden:** an E-Stop releases no handle. Brackets are stranded, so descriptors, pool connections and leases stay held until the process exits or recovery runs. It trades resource cleanliness for stop latency, which is the trade the button exists to make. **Not done:** the five non-py tiers keep their cooperative teardown and have no E-Stop — honest and visible rather than silently degraded; the formal layer is tier-independent so a later tier's loop builds against the same table.
444. **❌ OPEN, RE-VERIFIED IN SOURCE ON `bd0f4d19`: `src/revl/run.py:1096-1099` still carries the comment "The driver runs no taint analysis, so the digest gate is left fail-closed (`taint_engaged=False`)" and `:605` still defaults the parameter to `False`, so `runtime.revl_prompt_digest` (`backends/python/runtime.py:506`) returns `None` on every shipped run.** **THE ITEM-121 PROMPT DIGEST IS INERT IN THE SHIPPED DRIVER, AND THE COMPILE-TO-RUNTIME TAINT-ORIGIN CHANNEL IS NOT WIRED (2026-09-02, from item 416d's decision half).** The `revl trace` model-hop record carries a salted `promptDigest` whose ENTIRE point is a fail-closed suppression gate: `revl_prompt_digest` (`backends/python/runtime.py:500`) emits a digest ONLY when taint analysis is engaged AND proves the args carry neither a `secret` nor a `confidential` origin, and returns `None` otherwise. But the shipped driver (`run.py`, the emission-crossing record at `:1086`) passes `taint_engaged=False` UNCONDITIONALLY, with a comment stating the driver runs no taint analysis so the gate is left fail-closed. Consequence: in production the digest is ALWAYS suppressed, so the record never carries a `promptDigest` at all and the "same prompt twice" within-run equality the digest exists to provide is never available to a real run. **This is safe** (a suppressed digest leaks nothing, which is why item 416d fixed the reset half and consciously deferred this one rather than blocking on it): the surface is inert BY DESIGN, not broken. **What is missing is a feature, not a residue fix:** the checker computes per-arg taint origins (items 249/256), and nothing threads them to the runtime crossing record, so `_model_crossing_payload` has no `arg_origins` to hand `revl_prompt_digest` and no basis to set `taint_engaged=True`. Exit: decide whether the digest is worth having live at all (if not, state it as permanently inert and drop the machinery); if yes, wire a compile-to-runtime taint-origin channel (the checker's per-arg origins reach the driver's emission record, `taint_engaged` becomes true when the analysis is present) and add a test that a run with a proven-clean model arg emits a within-run-stable digest while a `secret`-tainted arg suppresses it end to end (today only `revl_prompt_digest` is unit-tested in isolation, `tests/test_trace_121.py`). Relates to 121 (the trace record), 249/256 (the taint origins), 416d (which fixed the reset and deferred this).

445. **THE UNIQUE-OWNERSHIP ANALYSIS BEHIND IN-PLACE ACCUMULATION IS WRITTEN TWICE AND IS FLOW-INSENSITIVE, WHICH LEAVES `list_sort` CUBIC AND `list_dedup` QUADRATIC (2026-09-02, from items 434 and 436 F1).** Two tiers now carry the SAME rule in different code: the go backend's `_v3_self_rebind_locals` (item 434 a/b/e) and the python backend's `_py_inplace_locals` (item 436 F1). Both say a local may be written in place exactly when the object it names is reachable through no other name, both prove it the same way (born from a fresh allocation here, every write a self-rebind, every other occurrence a non-retaining read, a parameter never eligible), and both were derived independently. Item 436's own fix note proposed the frontend `unique` marker for this reason; the two implementations are the evidence that it is worth doing, because ts, rust, java and wasm would each write it a third, fourth, fifth and sixth time. **Two gaps the flow-insensitive form leaves measurable, both reproducible with `PYTHONPATH=src python bench/codegen/python/run.py`:**
    (a) **Flow-insensitivity leaves `stdlib/list.rvl`'s `list_sort` at its emitted cubic.** Its inner accumulator is `var res = []` inside the outer loop, pushed into, then handed out with `out = res`. That last statement is an escape, so the analysis refuses the whole local; but the NEXT outer iteration re-declares `res` from a fresh literal, so the escaped object can never reach a later write and the rewrite would have been sound. Measured unchanged at 171700 copies at n=100 and 1353400 at n=200, x7.9 per doubling where the hand-written same-algorithm sort grows x4.0. Seeing it needs a forward may-alias pass with a fixpoint over the back edge (allocation sites as abstract objects; a fresh-literal birth KILLS the alias), which is a real dataflow analysis and was deliberately not attempted inside item 436.
    (b) **The rule closes over calls, so `list_dedup` stays quadratic.** `if (!list_contains(out, x)) { out = out.push(x) }` hands `out` to a call, and an intraprocedural analysis must assume a call retains its argument. `list_contains` demonstrably does not. A whole-program summary (does this fn retain any parameter) would answer it, and the same summary is what would let a local born from a CALL result (`var ys = list_map(xs, f)` then `ys = ys.push(z)`) be owned rather than refused. Note the python backend's existing template inliner already dissolves the SMALL cases by accident: a `sizeof(out)` that inlines to `len(out)` stops being a call before the analysis runs, which is why the gap only bites on fns too big to inline.
    **Exit:** decide first whether the marker belongs in the frontend (one analysis, `unique` on the IR node, six backends lowering it) or stays per-backend; if the frontend, the analysis must be checked against ts/rust/java/wasm for the same accumulation shape and ported to `selfhost/lower.rvl` with its IR-agreement oracle, which is the expensive half. Then (a), whose exit test is `transforms.list_sort` growing x4.0 per doubling instead of x7.9 in `bench/codegen/python/run.py`'s copy table, and (b), whose exit test is `list_dedup` growing x2.0. Both must keep every aliasing case in `tests/test_py_inplace_accumulation.py` green, since a wrong answer here is a silent aliasing bug and not a crash. Relates to 284 (rust's in-place self-append, the first tier to do this), 383 (the map/filter/reduce trio), 434, 436, 437(a).
    **DECIDED: THE FRONTEND, AND (a) AND (b) ARE BOTH CLOSED (2026-09-02, `feat/445-unique-ownership-marker`).** The decision is settled by what the rule is ABOUT rather than by tidiness: "is the object this binding names reachable through any other name" is a question about the SOURCE, and neither prior implementation consulted anything language-specific to answer it — both walk the same IR dicts and differ only in which builtins they trust. Three things followed that a per-backend copy could not have delivered. **(1) The marker is a FACT, not an instruction, and that is what makes it portable to six tiers that genuinely disagree about what to do with it.** `unique: true` on a self-rebinding `assign` says the binding owns its object at that write; each tier then decides. rust needs none of it (the borrow checker discharges the same obligation on the code that already compiles, item 437), no tier can mutate a `Str` (which is why `concat` is never marked and why go's item-434 (e) Builder exists), and a tier that ignores the marker keeps the copying form — always correct. go honours `true` only; python also honours `unique: "copy"`, the local born off another name (`var out = m`) that is owned because python materialises ONE defensive copy at the `let` marked `unique_birth: "List"|"Map"`, where the persistent form made one per write. A backend that does not implement that birth copy ignores those writes and stays correct, which is why the two flavours are separate values and not one boolean. **(2) Sharing it is what made PRECISION affordable, and the precision is the two gaps.** `src/revl/ownership.py` is a forward dataflow with a fixpoint on every loop back edge, asking the question PER WRITE instead of per name: a birth kills an escape, and a self-rebind kills it whichever form the backend picks (in place on a value nothing reaches, or the persistent copy's brand-new container), which is what makes the per-write question well-founded. A `return` needs no rule at all — the state after it is unreachable, so flow sensitivity subsumes the special case both prior versions had to state. On top of that a whole-program summary answers "does this fn retain parameter i", a least fixpoint over the call graph that starts optimistic and only adds retention. **(3) `selfhost/emit_py.rvl` got SMALLER**: it drops ~130 lines that were the reference analysis ported by hand, and reads two markers instead.
    **(a) CLOSED, and better than the exit test asked.** `bench/codegen/python/run.py`, `transforms.list_sort`: element copies **171700 -> 5050** at n=100 and **1353400 -> 20100** at n=200, so growth is **x7.9 -> x4.0** against the hand-written same-algorithm sort's x4.0 — and the absolute counts are now EQUAL to the hand arm, not merely the same growth class. `bytes` 4792/3200 = 1.50x -> **3200/3200 = 1.00x**. `ops` moves the other way, 1.26x -> 1.27x, because `append` is a method call where `+ [x]` is one binary op; that is the trade and it is the correct one, since `ops` is blind to the C-level copying `copies` exists to see.
    **(b) CLOSED, with the whole-program summary the item predicted.** `list_contains` walks its list and answers a Bool, so it retains nothing, and `list_dedup`'s push is owned. The bench grew a `transforms.deduped` case pinning it against the same algorithm by hand (a linear membership scan, so the number isolates the emitter's copying and not the algorithm): element copies **5050 -> 100** at n=200 and **20100 -> 200** at n=400, growth **x4.0 -> x2.0**, equal to the hand arm, with `ops` 1.00x and `bytes` 1.00x. Two summary rules differ from the local analysis and both follow from asking about the CALLER's object: a `return` RETAINS (a returned parameter is an alias by any definition), and a `for` ITERABLE does not (the iterator dies with the call, where inside one body it is held for the loop's whole extent).
    **THE CONSERVATIVE FALLBACK, stated because a wrong answer here is a silent aliasing bug and not a crash.** Every uncertainty resolves to "not owned", which emits the copying form the tiers had before. A parameter is never owned. A name is not owned until a birth this function made. An unmodelled statement shape kills every name in its subtree, and that fallback is deliberately blind to the retention summary. An expression slot not on the list retains. A builtin whose method is not on the whitelist is assumed to hand back an alias of its receiver — the whitelist is go's `_V3_LINEAR_READ_METHODS`, the NARROWER of the two merged rules and not their union, because `xs.slice(a, b)` is a fresh list on python and a header over the same backing array on go. Every callee without a summary retains every argument: an extern, a host root, a service method, a call through a function VALUE, a callee named by anything but a plain `var`, and any call whose argument count does not match the callee's parameter count.
    **LEFT OPEN: the `selfhost/lower.rvl` port, which is the expensive half the item named.** `lower.rvl` streams tokens straight to IR JSON in one pass and never builds the statement tree a forward dataflow with a loop fixpoint needs, so the native IR carries neither marker and diverges from the reference on any document with an accumulation loop — one in the emit_py corpus, `transforms.rvl`. Recorded as a NAMED strict-xfail (`UNIQUE_MARKER_GAP` in `tests/test_selfhost_lower_ir.py`) on the taint gap's terms: red for a stated reason, XPASSing loudly the day it is ported, rather than dropped from the corpus. The emit_py half DID land and is green. **ALSO LEFT: the four tiers not yet lowered.** ts (item 435 finding (d), `xs = xs.push(e)`, the tier that asked for this marker), java and wasm can each read `unique` now and were not audited here; rust deliberately never will. And the summary's other use the item noted — a local born from a CALL result (`var ys = list_map(xs, f)` then `ys = ys.push(z)`) being owned rather than refused — needs a FRESHNESS summary ("is this fn's result newly allocated and unaliased"), which is a different question from retention and was not attempted.

    **ts LOWERED (2026-09-03, PR #262), which closes item 435 (d) — the finding that asked for this marker.** `backends/typescript/emit.py` reads `"unique": true` and renders `push` / `set` / `remove` / a record update destructively; `"unique": "copy"` is declined there because its `unique_birth` shape `"Map"` covers both a revl `Map` (a JS `Map`) and a record update (a plain object), so the birth copy has no single spelling on that tier. Measured: elements copied building an n-element list go 79800 -> 0 at n=400, equal to hand-written, with microtask turns and Promise allocations unchanged. `selfhost/emit_ts.rvl` ported; the native-chain half hits the SAME `lower.rvl` gap as the py tier and is now a named strict-xfail there too (`NATIVE_UNIQUE_MARKER_GAP` in `tests/test_selfhost_compile.py`, `ts:transforms.rvl`). Full detail under item 435 (d). **java AND wasm ARE STILL NOT LOWERED, and each was taken to a concrete blocker rather than left unexamined.** **java: the container the marker points at is IMMUTABLE.** `var xs = []` emits `java.util.List xs = java.util.List.of()` and `revlPush` returns `Stream.concat(..).toList()`, so `xs.add(v)` throws; and because the marker is flow-sensitive a name can be unowned at one write and owned at the next, which would land an in-place write on the immutable result of the preceding persistent one. A sound lowering therefore needs a per-name gate (every write to this name marked AND every birth a literal this tier can make mutable) plus mutable births, which changes the declared type of accumulator locals on a tier whose comments record that choice being tuned twice already (`_let_keyword`'s raw `java.util.List` for an untyped `[]`, and item 433 F8 moving `maplit` FROM `new HashMap<>()` TO `Map.of()`). Separately the java Map accumulator DOES NOT COMPILE today: with `JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk`, `var m = Map.empty()` infers `Map<Object,Object>` and `javac` rejects both `revlMapSet(Map<Object,Object>, String, long)` and `return m` against a declared `Map<String, Long>` — a pre-existing red that any java lowering lands on top of. The instrument exists (`bench/codegen/java`, allocated bytes per op via `getCurrentThreadAllocatedBytes`; `list_push` measures 221224 B/op emitted against 286760 hand), but its `Hand.java` is a PERSISTENT yardstick by design, so the win needs a new mutable-arm case. **wasm: the list header has no capacity field, so there is nowhere to append.** `$list_push` is `[i32 count][8-byte slots]` and `$alloc`s a fresh region plus a `memory.copy` on every push; an in-place append needs either a capacity field (a layout change reaching `$list_concat`, `$list_slice`, indexing, length and the canonical ABI) or a bump-allocator adjacency trick. Neither is a marker-reading change. Both tiers keep the copying form, which is correct.

446. **DEAD TEST SWITCHES: A CORRECT SUITE GATED BEHIND AN ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE NOBODY SETS IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A PASSING ONE, AND THIS IS THE SECOND KNOWN INSTANCE (2026-09-02).** A skip and a pass are the same colour on a dashboard, so a suite that is written, correct, and gated behind a switch that is set in no workflow, no Makefile and no `ci/` script reports green forever while measuring nothing. **Two instances are already on this roadmap and neither was found by looking for the class**; both were found by tripping over a defect the dead suite already covered. Item **430**: `pytest tests/` ran in exactly one job, which installed no cordis-py, so 398 tests across 81 modules executed nowhere in CI. Item **433**: `REVL_CROSS_TIER_SLOW` was set nowhere, so the rust and java halves of the cross-tier semantic floor executed nowhere, and riders R1 (`Int / Int` doing Java integer division) and R2 (`==` on Float going through `doubleToLongBits`, inverting NaN and `-0.0`) survived under `IEEE_FLOAT` assertions that had covered them since Float landed. Java has never executed that file. The skip counted as a pass.

    **THE AUDIT, verified rather than assumed.** Genuine environment gates in `tests/`, cross-referenced against `.github/workflows/`, `Makefile` and `ci/`. `REVL_CROSS_TIER_SLOW`: **17 `skipif` decorators across TWO files, not one**, 16 in `tests/test_cross_tier_execution.py` and a 17th in `tests/test_time_coeffect.py` (`test_rust_async_timer_lifecycle_runs_end_to_end`), which every prior count of this switch missed because it sits in an unrelated file; NEVER SET. `REVL_CONFORMANCE_TS`, `REVL_CONFORMANCE_PY`, `CORDIS_WASM`: never set, but all three are **OVERRIDES, not gates**: each falls back to an in-repo path and the real gate is a filesystem probe, so "never set" is the correct state for them and the audit's headline count of four dead switches is really ONE dead switch plus three overrides. `REVL_PY` and `REVL_REQUIRE_WASMTIME` are genuinely set, each in exactly ONE place, both in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the `conformance` and `backend-wasm` jobs respectively); `ci/placement_smoke.sh` only READS `REVL_PY` as a `${REVL_PY:-...}` fallback, which proves nothing about the variable being set, and the guard below deliberately does not count a read as a set for that reason. `REVL_ORDER_LOG`, `REVL_WIT_TARGET` and `REVL_SECRET_API_KEY` are set by the suite itself (`monkeypatch.setenv`, or handed to emitted code) and are not switches at all.

    **A THIRD GATE, FOUND WHILE MEASURING, AND IT IS NOT AN ENV VAR.** `RUNNERS["ts"]` requires `backends/typescript/node_modules/.bin/vitest`, and **no CI job that runs `tests/` executes `npm ci`**, neither `frontend`, not `frontend-cordis`. So the TypeScript tier of the cross-tier suite has skipped in CI exactly as hard as java did, while the file's header, `docs/contract-errata.md` and `docs/arithmetic.md` all described it as executing "by default". This is the same class with a filesystem probe in place of an environment variable, which is why item 433's sweep for dead env switches could not see it, and why the guard below states plainly that it does not catch this half.

    **A THIRD INSTANCE, AND THE VARIANT MOST LIKELY TO SURVIVE A REVIEW: RIGHT VARIABLE, WRONG JOB.** `REVL_CORDIS4J_CLASSES` IS set in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, so every audit that asks "is this switch set anywhere in CI" answers yes and moves on. It is set in the `backend-java` job, which runs `backends/java/test_emit_java.py` and nothing else. The test that READS it is `tests/test_realm_conformance.py::test_cordis4j_realm_conformance`, and every job that collects `tests/` (`frontend`, `frontend-cordis`, and this item's new `conformance` step) leaves it unset. So that probe has skipped in CI as completely as the `REVL_CROSS_TIER_SLOW` ones, while looking fully provisioned. This is item 430's shape exactly, a third time. NOT CLOSED: closing it means cloning and compiling cordis4j-core in `conformance` the way `backend-java` already does, and that step could not be executed on the audit machine to prove it green first. It is enumerated instead, in the `conformance` job comment and in the guard's `_KNOWN_WRONG_JOB` registry, so it cannot go quiet.

    **MEASURED, on an arm64 laptop, `tests/test_cross_tier_execution.py` alone.** Default gates: **30s**, 93 pass, 94 skip. With `node_modules` present: **3m53**, 128 pass. Plus `REVL_CROSS_TIER_SLOW=1` so rust executes: **4m53**, 156 pass. Plus a working JDK so java executes: **6m31**, 180 pass, 5 skip. **87 tests newly execute** across those three gates. The file was NOT narrowed to make that fit: a smaller green is what created this item.

    **THE FULL MATRIX WAS RUN, AND IT PRODUCES EXACTLY ONE FAILURE.** `/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk` (JDK 26) is installed on the audit machine but keg-only, so it is absent from `PATH` and `_java_tool`'s `shutil.which("javac")` finds only the macOS shim. **That is why item 433 states "no JDK on this machine" and took no java measurement at all; that premise was wrong, and putting the keg-only bin directory on `PATH` is the whole fix.** With it, the complete five-tier matrix runs, item 433's R1 and R2 fixes execute green on a real JVM for the first time, and the single failure is `test_probe_executes_identically_slow[java-structural equality]`: `_emit_v3_types` (`backends/java/emit.py`) emits a v3 record as a bare `public static final class` with no `equals`/`hashCode`, so `Objects.equals` on two equal records is Object identity and false. That is the gap item 433's rider section already recorded, landed via `fix/433-java-record-equality` (`2d55c746`: v3 records and variant cases got a structural `equals`/`hashCode`, primitives comparing with primitive `==` and references through `revlEq`, hashing through `revlHash`). That closes the one failure blocking this flip and nothing wider: the rest of item 433's java findings stay open under issue #70. **Nothing else fails.** The flip is therefore proven safe the moment that lands, which is a stronger statement than "it should work".

    **DONE.** (a) The `conformance` job, the one place node, rust, java, go and wasmtime all exist at once and the only job that runs `npm ci`, now runs `tests/test_cross_tier_execution.py`, `tests/test_realm_conformance.py` and `tests/test_time_coeffect.py` under the cordis-py venv. That alone closes the TypeScript hole and the `REVL_CONFORMANCE_TS` / `REVL_CONFORMANCE_PY` holes, and needs no java fix. (b) The `REVL_CROSS_TIER_SLOW=1` flip sits in that same step **commented out, with the failing probe named**, staged behind the java record fix. The probe is not deselected and the file is not narrowed. (c) The false prose is gone: `tests/test_total_field_surface.py` claimed "CI runs the full matrix" and `docs/contract-errata.md` claimed TypeScript executes by default; both now say what actually runs where. (d) **The systemic guard**, `tests/test_env_gated_skips_run_somewhere.py`: it AST-scans `tests/` for every environment name the suite READS but never SETS (resolving indirections like `_TARGET_ENV = "REVL_WIT_TARGET"`, and not counting a subprocess `env` dict as ownership), and fails unless each one is either assigned somewhere in `.github/workflows/`, `ci/` or the `Makefile`, or listed in an `_INTENTIONALLY_LOCAL` registry with a reason. Commented-out lines do not count as set. The registry may only shrink: a separate test fails if an entry stops being read or starts being set in CI, and a third rejects a reason under 80 characters or one that amounts to "it is slow", because slow is what a dedicated job is for. A fourth check, `test_a_ci_set_gate_is_set_in_a_job_that_actually_runs_it`, closes the right-variable-wrong-job variant: for every BARE read (no default, so nothing but CI can supply a value) it parses the pytest targets out of each workflow step that sets the variable and requires one of them to actually collect a file that reads it. Verified non-vacuous by clearing the registry and watching it name `REVL_CORDIS4J_CLASSES`.

    **THE GUARD IS ITSELF STAGED, AND ON PURPOSE.** Its main assertion is marked `xfail(strict=True)` today, since `REVL_CROSS_TIER_SLOW` really is still unset. The moment somebody uncomments the two lines in `ci.yml` the test PASSES, which under `strict` is a FAILURE, so whoever lands the java fix cannot avoid returning to delete the marker. Parking the name in `_INTENTIONALLY_LOCAL` with an excuse would have gone quiet instead, which is the precise failure mode this item exists to stop. **Verified by simulating the flip: uncommenting makes it red with `[XPASS(strict)]`, and reverting makes it xfail again.**

    **EXIT, for whoever lands `fix/433-java-record-equality`.** Uncomment the two `env:` lines in the `conformance` job, delete the `xfail` marker in `tests/test_env_gated_skips_run_somewhere.py`, confirm the full file is green on the runner, and tick this item. **Until then, and generally: a `*_slow` skip means UNMEASURED, never passing.** Relates to 430 (the same shape, one job away) and 433 (the two live defects it hid).

    **A FOURTH GATE, AND IT LEFT THE REGISTRY INSTEAD OF JOINING IT (`CORDIS_WASM`, PR #197).** `_INTENTIONALLY_LOCAL` carried `CORDIS_WASM` with the reason that the cordis-wasm substrate is a separate repository and a prototype, so pinning its revision would be "a decision, not an oversight". Widening `backend-wasm` from one named file to the whole root made the cost of that decision visible: NINETEEN newly-collected tests — router, spawn and accessor execution, str-literal length, the lifecycle driver — skipped on "cordis-wasm runtime not found", and the job's own no-skip guard reddened on them, correctly. The decision was taken rather than deferred: the job now clones cordis-wasm at the pin `f5c0562` and builds the venv `tests/test_wasm_backend.py` resolves by absolute path, declares `CORDIS_WASM` as a JOB env so `test_a_ci_set_gate_is_set_in_a_job_that_actually_runs_it` can check that the job setting it is the job collecting those files, and the registry entry is DELETED — `test_no_stale_local_declarations` would fail otherwise, which is the registry-may-only-shrink rule doing exactly what it was written for. TWELVE of the nineteen now execute. The other SEVEN are VERSION gates, not switch gates: the pinned runtime predates the instance accessor (`_instance_get`, 2 tests) and the `route:<key>` primitive (item 173, 5 tests), and no change in this repo can make them run — the primitives have to reach the cordis-wasm repo's `main` and the pin has to be bumped. Both reasons are enumerated verbatim in the guard's `ALLOWED` list, so bumping the pin makes them fail as stale rather than keeping a dead exemption alive, and nothing else can hide behind them. The guard also had to stop comparing raw XML: a reason carrying `<key>` reaches the junit report as `&lt;key&gt;`, so an exemption spelled in plain text would silently never have matched.

451. **A MERGE THAT KEEPS BOTH SIDES OF A ROADMAP HUNK IS INVISIBLE, AND IT HAS HAPPENED THREE TIMES (2026-09-02).** Found while attaching owners to the orphan findings. Git resolves a conflicting roadmap hunk by keeping both sides; prose has no syntax that makes that a build error, so the duplicate just sits there and the FIRST copy is the one a reader believes. Three instances on main, all from the same week: **(a) ✅ FIXED HERE.** Merge `bd0f4d19` kept a stale `106. 🚧` header line above the `106. ✅` entry that `38c84207` had replaced, identical apart from the marker and with no body of its own. That one line was the only reason a landed item read as in-progress, and it is what `--check-duplicate-headers` (added in the same commit, `tools/check_roadmap_markers.py::duplicate_header_findings`) now catches. **(b) ❌ STILL OPEN, item 428.** Merge `9e7e551b` kept both sides of item 428's finding set, so F5-F13 are written TWICE: the reconciliation pass `599120ef` (re-verified at `bd0f4d19`, before the fixes landed) and `fix/428-attestation-tail`'s own updates. Both sets now carry the same verdict and the same shas after the ownership sweep, so no reader is misled, but the item still says everything twice. **(c) ❌ STILL OPEN, item 433.** Same shape: F1-F10 appear once with `❌ STILL OPEN, RE-VERIFIED IN SOURCE ON bd0f4d19` heads and once as the original audit text, plus the correctness-riders panel twice at 8.9 kB and 13.9 kB. **THE GAP THE NEW CHECK DOES NOT CLOSE.** `--check-duplicate-headers` asks the question per ITEM NUMBER, so it sees (a) and is blind to (b) and (c), which duplicate F-BLOCKS inside one item. The same question one level down — one F label carrying two blocks in one item — is decidable from the file alone and is the natural extension. **WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS.** Item 428's stale copy said F7/F8/F10/F11/F13 were STILL OPEN, re-verified in source, with line numbers; every one of them had been fixed and merged three hours later. A reader who trusted it would have re-audited five closed findings, which is the same cost item 99 and item 107 paid, and item 100 and item 112, and 101/113, 102/114, 103/115. 452. **THE ISSUE MIGRATION SKIPPED EIGHT OPEN ITEMS, AND `--require-issue` CANNOT BE TURNED ON UNTIL IT IS FINISHED (2026-09-02).** `python3 tools/check_roadmap_markers.py --require-issue` reports 59 open/partial items citing no GitHub issue. Fifty-one of those have an issue on the tracker and simply do not cite it in their own text, which is a mechanical fix. The other EIGHT have no issue at all: items 5, 10, 416, 421, 422, 425, 427 and 428. 453. **A DEMO THAT IS TYPECHECKED BUT NEVER RUN IS PROSE, AND THE TS TIER'S HAD BEEN WRONG SINCE AUGUST (2026-09-02, FIXED IN PR #243).** `node demo.ts` failed one check on main: `R2 - reactivated cache runs its effects afresh (new store)`. The assertion read `ctx.cache.get('alice') === null` and it was CORRECT when written - at `ebf7cba0` the ts runtime's `MapHandle.get` answered `this.data.get(key) ?? null`. `cabbd931` dropped that `?? null` deliberately and correctly, because `Opt` is bare `value | undefined` on this tier, `emit.py` lowers `match` over an Opt by discriminating on `=== undefined`, and a `null` answer made `None == None` false through `revlEq`. That commit updated `emit.py`, `runtime.ts` and `tests/test_lifecycle.py`. It did not update the demo, which has asserted something impossible ever since.

    **THE DIVERGENCE WAS NOT CROSS-TIER, WHICH IS WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE THE FAILURE LOOKED LIKE ONE.** All six tiers agree on an absent key and each answers its own native `Opt` None: python `None`, ts `undefined`, rust `Option::None`, java `Optional.empty()`, go a nil `*T` ("Opt lowers to a pointer `*T` (nil == None)"), wasm a tag-0 cell. The source is `fn get(key: Str) -> Opt[Str]`; nothing in the emitter or the runtime was wrong and the fix belonged in the demo. It was made `=== undefined` and NOT `== null` on purpose: on this tier `null` is not None, so the loose spelling would wave through precisely the regression `cabbd931` fixed.

    **THE TRAP IS THAT THE TYPECHECK DID COVER THE FILE.** `backend-typescript` ran vitest, `scripts/typecheck-generated.mjs` and `tsc --noEmit`, and `tsconfig.json` includes `demo.ts`. So the demo was type-correct and green for the whole period its assertions were never evaluated. Typechecking a demo proves it compiles; only running it proves it still demonstrates anything. `backend-python` runs `.venv/bin/python demo.py`, and that is the entire reason the python demo has not rotted - not that it is better written. The ts tier now has the same property via an unconditional `node demo.ts` step (no `if:`, no env gate, no optional toolchain; the demo already exits non-zero on a failed check), held there by `tests/test_ts_demo_runs_in_ci.py` in the shape of `test_ts_typecheck_gate_runs_in_ci.py` - static, no toolchain, running in `frontend`, because a runtime probe would live inside the very job that might stop running the step. Verified non-vacuous by deleting the step and watching three of its four checks go red.

    **CONFORMANCE DOES NOT COVER THE QUESTION EITHER, AND THAT ABSENCE IS THE SECOND FINDING.** `tools/conformance.py` emits every case per tier and hands the artifacts to `tools/validate.py`, whose validators stop at compile/typecheck depth - `tsc`, `cargo check`, `javac + cordis4j stubs`, `go build`, `wasmtime compile`, and the empty depth for python. Not one of them EXECUTES. So `Map.get`'s null/undefined answer is not a conformance claim: the matrix proves a construct emits and the artifact compiles, never what it evaluates to. A cross-tier value question cannot be answered by that corpus as it stands.

    **THE SURVEY, since the same question was owed to the other five tiers.** There are exactly three tier demos. `backends/python/demo.py` runs in `backend-python`. `backends/typescript/demo.ts` ran nowhere and now runs here. `backends/wasm/demo.py` is invoked by `tests/test_wasm_backend.py::test_demo_runs_on_the_real_substrate` under `skipif(not CORDIS_WASM_PY.exists())` - and `"cordis-wasm venv not available"` is the single string in the `ALLOWED` exemption of the `backend-wasm` job's own "no wasm test may skip in CI" guard, so CI never provisions the substrate and that demo has never executed there. go, rust and java have no demo at all. **LEFT OPEN: the wasm half**, which is this item's shape sitting inside a deliberate allowance rather than an oversight, and which needs the cordis-wasm substrate in CI to close. Relates to 430 and 446 (a skip and a pass are the same colour), issue #183 (one named test file per job, so whole suites never executed) and issue #191 (the release path never exercised).

454. ✅ **CONFORMANCE PROVED COMPILATION AND WAS READ AS PROVING BEHAVIOUR; IT NOW EXECUTES 19 OF ITS 61 CASES AND COMPARES THE ANSWERS ACROSS TIERS (2026-09-03, LANDED IN PR #258, issue #244).** Item 453's second finding, closed for the tiers that already have a runtime in CI. Every validator in `tools/validate.py` stopped at compile or typecheck depth - `tsc`, `cargo check`, `javac`, `go build`, `wasmtime compile`, and a syntax + unbound-name walk for python - so the matrix certified that a construct emits and compiles per tier and never what it evaluates to. Two tiers could be green on the same case and disagree about the answer, which is not hypothetical: java typechecked `Int / Int` cleanly while answering 3 where every other tier answered 3.5 (item 433 rider R1), and `tsc --noEmit` covered `backends/typescript/demo.ts` for the whole period its runtime assertions were failing (item 453).

    **WHAT LANDED.** `tools/validate.py` gains `EXECUTORS` for python (in-process), typescript (vitest) and go (`go test`), the three tiers whose runtime the `conformance` job already provisions. `python3 tools/conformance.py --execute` runs the executable half of the corpus on each and reports agreement per case, exiting non-zero on a disagreement; `--require-execution` also fails when an executed tier's runtime is absent, so CI cannot quietly demote those rows to compile-only; `--check-toolchains` now reports the executed tiers alongside the compile validators, because a missing vitest is a broken job for the same reason a missing `javac` is. `make matrix-execute` is the local entry point, and the `conformance` job gains one step. No job was renamed.

    **IT IS A DIFFERENTIAL, NOT A PER-TIER SMOKE TEST**, because a per-tier "it ran" is only marginally better than "it compiled". Each executable case carries a `probe()` and ONE answer written as a revl literal (`tools/conformance.py::PROBES`); the executed program is the unchanged case plus that probe plus `test "conformance_answer" { assert probe() == <answer> }`, and every executed tier asserts the SAME literal. So the only way to fail is to build, run, and compute something else - and because the answer is authored rather than read off whichever tier ran first, three tiers quietly agreeing on a wrong value fails too. `expr/Int32 bitwise` is the sharpest probe: `mask(6, 6, 2)` is -1, which separates an arithmetic `>>` from a logical `>>>` and a 32-bit lane from a 64-bit one. Proved non-vacuous by `test_a_wrong_answer_is_caught` and by hand: a deliberately wrong `expr/true division` literal reports `differs` on all three tiers, python naming the values (`left = 3.5, right = 3.0`).

    **THE SPLIT: 19 EXECUTED, 42 COMPILE-ONLY, of the 61 cases the frontend admits.** A uniform-looking table over two claim strengths is how the absence stayed invisible, so the generated matrix now carries a **claim** column per row plus a per-claim summary. The 42 are not a to-do list; they are cases whose value a pure call cannot reach: 9 `signature` cases (`type/*` declares a shape and computes nothing) and 33 `activation` cases (the value is produced inside a component provide-method, or during activation via `effect`, `emit` or an `acquire` extern). Reaching those means booting the composition on each tier's runtime, which `ci/placement_smoke.sh` and `revl run --placement` already do, so that is the natural next tranche. All three executed tiers agree on all 19 today. The claim column is corpus data, so it regenerates byte-identically anywhere and the existing `--check-readme` staleness gate covers it; whether the executed rows agreed is the `--execute` step, gated separately.

    **HELD BY** `tests/test_conformance_execution.py`: the differential per tier (a tier with no runtime skips with its own reason, never passes), the negative control, that every probe program still compiles, and the bookkeeping that keeps every admitted case in exactly one claim bucket with a reason. **LEFT OPEN:** rust, java and wasm still stop at compile depth here, and the `activation` tranche needs the placement runners. `docs/conformance.md`'s refusal table is separately stale (issue #233) and was not touched.
